speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: You are welcome to your country, dear Antonio ; You have been long in France, and you return A very formal Frenchman in your habit : How do you like the French court ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I admire it : In seeking to reduce both state and people To a fix'd order, their judicious king Begins at home ; quits first his royal palace Of flattering sycophants, of dissolute And infamous persons, — which he sweetly terms His master's master-piece, the work of heaven ; Considering duly that a prince's court Is like a common fountain, whence should flow A Pure silver drops in general, but if 't chance Some curs'd example poison 't near the head, Death and diseases through the whole land spread. And what *s '* makes this blessed government But a most provident council, who dare freely Inform him the corruption of the times ? Though some o' the court hold it presumption ' , To instruct princes what they ought to do, It is a noble duty to inform them What they ought to foresee. — Here comes Bosola, The only court-gall ; yet I observe his railing Is not for simple love of piety : Indeed, he rails at those things which he wants ; Would be as lecherous, covetous, or proud, Bloody, or envious, as any man, If he had means to be so.— Here 's the cardinal.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I do haunt you still.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: So.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I have done you better service than to be slighted thus. Miserable age, where only the reward of doing well is the doing of it !

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: You enforce your merit too much.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I fell into the galleys in your service ; where, for two years together, I wore two towels instead of a shirt, with a knot on the shoulder, after the fashion of a Roman mantle. Slighted thus ! I will thrive some way : black-birds fatten best in hard weather ; why not I in these dog-days ?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Would you could become honest !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: With all your divinity do but direct me the way to it. I have known many travel far for it, and yet return as arrant knaves as they went forth, because they carried themselves always along with them. Are you gone? Some fellows, they say, are possessed with the devil, but this great fellow were able to possess the greatest devil, and make him worse.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: He hath denied thee some suit !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: He and his brother are like plum-trees that grow crooked over standing-pools ; they are rich and o'erladen with fruit, but none but crows, pies, and caterpillars feed on them. Could I be one of their flattering panders, I would hang on their ears like a horseleech, till I were full, and then drop off. I pray, leave me. Who would rely upon these miserable dependencies, in expectation to be advanced to-morrow? what creature ever fed worse than hoping Tantalus ? nor ever died any man more fearfully than he that hoped for a pardon. There are rewards for hawks and dogs when they have done us service ; but for a soldier that hazards his limbs in a battle, nothing but a kind of geometry is his last supportation.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Geometry !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Ay, to hang in a fair pair of slings, take his latter swing in the world upon an honourable pair of crutches, from hospital to hospital. Fare ye well, sir : and yet do not you scorn us ; for places in the court are but like beds in the hospital, where this man's head lies at that man's foot, and so lower and lower.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I knew this fellow seven years in the galleys For a notorious murder ; and 'twas thought The cardinal suborn'd it : he was releas'd By the French general, Gaston de Foix, When he recover'd Naples.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Tis great pity He should be thus neglected : I have heard He's very valiant. This foul melancholy Will poison all his goodness ; for, I '11 tell you, If too immoderate sleep be truly said To be an inward rust unto the soul, It then doth follow want of action Breeds all black malcontents ; and their close rearing, Like moths in cloth, do hurt for want of wearing.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: The presence 'gins to fill : you promis'd me To make me the partaker of the natures Of some of your great courtiers.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: The lord cardinal's And other strangers' that are now in court ? I shall. — Here comes the great Calabrian duke.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Who took the ring oftenest ?

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: Antonio Bologna, my lord.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Our sister duchess' great-master of her household ? give him the jewel. — When shall we leave this sportive action, and fall to action indeed ?

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: Methinks, my lord, you should not desire to go to war in person.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Now for some gravity : — why, my lord ?

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: It is fitting a soldier arise to be a prince, but not necessary a prince descend to be a captain.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: No.

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: No, my lord ; he were far better do it by a deputy.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Why should he not as well sleep or eat by a deputy? this might take idle, offensive, and base office from him, whereas the other deprives him of honour.

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: Believe my experience, that realm is never long in quiet where the ruler is a soldier.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Thou toldest me thy wife could not endure fighting.

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: True, my lord.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: And of a jest she broke of a captain she met full of wounds : I have forgot it.

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: She told him, my lord, he was a pitiful fellow, to lie, like the children of Ismael, all in tents.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Why, there's a wit were able to undo all the chirurgeons o' the city ; for although gallants should quarrel, and had drawn their weapons, and were ready to go to it, yet her persuasions would make them put up.

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: That she would, my lord.— How do you like my Spanish gennet ?

speeches.speaker: RODERIGO
speeches.text: He is all fire.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I am of Pliny's opinion, I think he was begot by the wind ; he runs as if he were ballassed with quicksilver.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: True, my lord, he reels from the tilt often.

speeches.speaker: RODERIGO AND GRISOLAN
speeches.text: Ha, ha, ha !

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Why do you laugh? methinks you that are courtiers should be my touch-wood, take fire when I give fire ; that is, laugh [but] when I laugh, were the subject never so witty.

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: True, my lord : I myself have heard a very good jest, and have scorned to seem to have so silly a wit as to understand it.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: But I can laugh at your fool, my lord.

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: He cannot speak, you know, but he makes faces : my lady cannot abide him.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: No?

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: Nor endure to be in merry company ; for she says too much laughing, and too much company, fills her too full of the wrinkle.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I would, then, have a mathematical instrument made for herface, that she might not laugh out of compass.—I shall shortly visit you at Milan, Lord Silvio.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: Your grace shall arrive most welcome.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You are a good horseman, Antonio : you have excellent riders in France : what do you think of good horsemanship ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Nobly, my lord : as out of the Grecian horse issued many famous princes, so out of brave horsemanship arise the first sparks of growing resolution, that raise the mind to noble action.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You have bespoke it worthily.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: Your brother, the lord cardinal, and sister duchess.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Are the galleys come about ?

speeches.speaker: GRISOLAN
speeches.text: They are, my lord.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Here 's the Lord Silvio is come to take his leave.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Now, sir,ryour promise : what 's that cardinal ? I mean his temper ? they say he 's a brave fellow, Will play his five thousand crowns at tennis, dance, Court ladies, and one that hath fought single combats.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Some such flashes superficially hang on him for form ; but observe his inward character : he is a melancholy churchman ; the spring in his face is nothing but the engendering of toads ; where he is jealous of any man, he lays worse plots for them than ever was imposed on Hercules, for he strews in his way flatterers, panders, intelligencers, atheists, and a thousand such political monsters. He should have been Pope ; but instead of coming to it by the primitive decency of the church, he did bestow bribes so largely and so impudently as if he would have carried it away without heaven's knowledge. Some good he hath done

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: You have given too much of him. What 's his brother ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: The duke there? a most perverse and turbulent nature : What appears in him mirth is merely outside ; If he laught heartily, it is to laugh All honesty out of fashion.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Twins?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: In quality. He speaks with others' tongues, and hears men's suits With others' ears ; will seem to sleep o' the bench Only to entrap offenders in their answers ; Dooms men to death by information ; Rewards by hearsay.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Then the law to him Is like a foul, black cobweb to a spider, — He makes it his dwelling and a prison To entangle those shall feed him.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Most true : He never pays debts unless they be shrewd turns, And those he will confess that he doth owe. Last, for his brother there, the cardinal, They that do flatter him most say oracles Hang at his lips ; and verily I believe them, For the devil speaks in them. But for their sister, the right noble duchess, You never fix'd your eye on three fair medals Cast in one figure, of so different temper. For her discourse, it is so full of rapture, You only will begin then to be sorry When she doth end her speech, and wish, in wonder, She held it less vain-glory to talk much, Than your penance to hear her : whilst she speaks, She throws upon a man so sweet a look, That it were able to raise one to a galliard That lay in a dead palsy, and to dote On that sweet countenance ; but in that look There speaketh so divine a continence j As cuts off all lascivious and vain hope. Her days are practis'd in such noble virtue, That sure her nights, nay, more, her very sleeps, Are more in heaven than other ladies' shrifts. Let all sweet ladies break their flattering glasses, And dress themselves in her.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Fie, Antonio, You play the wire-drawer with her commendations.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I '11 case the picture up : only thus much ; All her particular worth grows to this sum, — She stains the time past, lights the time to come.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: You must attend my lady in the gallery, Some half an hour hence.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I shall.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Sister, I have a suit to you.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: To me, sir ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: A gentleman here, Daniel de Bosola, One that was in the galleys

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Yes, I know him.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: A worthy fellow he is : pray, let me entreat for The provisorship of your horse.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Your knowledge of him Commends him and prefers him.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Call him hither. We [are] now upon parting. Good Lord Silvio, Do us commend to all our noble friends At the leaguer.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: Sir, I shall.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You are for Milan ?

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: I am.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Bring the caroches.— We '11 bring you down to the haven.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Be sure you entertain that Bosola For your intelligence : I would not be seen in 't ; And therefore many times I have slighted him When he did court our furtherance, as this morning.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Antonio, the great-master of her household, Had been far fitter.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: You are deceiv'd in him His nature is too honest for such business.— He comes : I '11 leave you.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I was lur'd to you.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: My brother, here, the cardinal could never Abide you.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Never since he was in my debt.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: May be some oblique character in your face Made him suspect you.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Doth he study physiognomy ? There 's no more credit to be given to the face Than to a sick man's urine, which some call The physician's whore because she cozens him. He did suspect me wrongfully.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: For that You must give great men leave to take their times. Distrust doth cause us seldom be deceiv'd : You see the oft shaking of the cedar-tree Fastens it more at root.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yet, take heed ; For to suspect a friend unworthily Instructs him the next way to suspect you, And prompts him to deceive you.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: There 's gold.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: So: What follows ? never rained such showers as these ii Without thunderbolts i' the tail of them : whose throat must I cut ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Your inclination to shed blood rides post Before my occasion to use you. I give you that To live i' the court here, and observe the duchess ; To note all the particulars of her haviour, What suitors do solicit her for marriage, And whom she best affects. She 's a young widow : I would not have her marry again.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: No, sir?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Do not you ask the reason ; but be satisfied. I say I would not.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: It seems you would create me One of your familiars.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Familiar ! what Js that ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Why, a very quaint invisible devil in flesh, — An intelligencer.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Such a kind of thriving thing I would wish thee ; and ere long thou mayst arrive At a higher place by 't.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Take your devils, Which hell calls angels : these curs'd gifts would make You a corrupter, me an impudent traitor : And should I take these, they 'd take me [to] hell.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Sir, I'll take nothing from you that I have given : There is a place that I procured for you This morning, the provisorship o' the horse ; Have you heard on 't ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: No.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: 'Tis yours : is 't not worth thanks ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I would have you curse yourself now, that your bounty (Which makes men truly noble) e'er should make me A villain. O, that to avoid ingratitude For the good deed you have done me, I must do All the ill man can invent ! Thus the devil Candies all sins o'er ; and what heaven terms vile, That names he complimental.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Be yourself; Keep your old garb of melancholy ; 'twill express You envy those that stand above your reach, Yet strive not to come near 'em : this will gain Access to private lodgings, where yourself May, like a politic dormouse '_ .

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: As I have seen some Feed in a lord's dish, half asleep, not seeming To listen to any talk ; and yet these rogues Have cut his throat in a dream. What 's my place ? The provisorship o' the horse? say, then, my corruption Grew out of horse-dung : I am your creature.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Away !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Let good men, for good deeds, covet good fame, Since place and riches oft are bribes of shame : Sometimes the devil doth preach.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: We are to part from you; and your own discretion Must now be your director.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You are a widower You know already what man is ; and therefore Let not youth, high promotion, eloquence

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: No, Nor anything without the addition, honour, Sway your high blood.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Marry ! they are most luxurious Will wed twice.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: O, fie !

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Their livers are more spotted Than Laban's sheep.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Diamonds are of most value, They say, that have pass'd through most jewellers' hands.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Whores by that rule are precious.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Will you hear me ? I '11 never marry.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: So most widows say ; But commonly that motion lasts no longer Than the turning of an hour-glass : the funeral sermon And it end both together.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Now hear me : You live in a rank pasture, here, i' the court ; There is a kind of honey-dew that 's deadly ; 'Twill poison your fame ; look to 't : be not cunning; For they whose faces do belie their hearts Are witches ere they arrive at twenty years, Ay, and give the devil suck.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: This is terrible good counsel.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Hypocrisy is woven of a fine small thread, Subtler than Vulcan's engine : yet, believe 't, Your darkest actions, nay, your privat'st thoughts, Will come to light.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: You may flatter yourself, And take your own choice ; privately be married Under the eaves of night

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Think 't the best voyage That e'er you made ; like the irregular crab, Which, though 't goes backward, thinks that it goes right Because it goes its own way : but observe, Such weddings may more properly be said To be executed than celebrated.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: The marriage night Is the entrance into some prison.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: And those joys, Those lustful pleasures, are like heavy sleeps Which do fore-run man's mischief.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Fare you well. Wisdom begins at the end : remember it.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I think this speech between you both was studied, It came so roundly off.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You are my sister ; This was my father's poniard, do you see ? I 'd be loth to see Jt look rusty, 'cause 'twas his. I would have you give o'er these chargeable revels : A visor and a mask are whispering-rooms That were never built for goodness ; — fare ye well ; — And women like that part which, like the lamprey, Hath never a bone in 't.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Fie, sir!

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Nay, I mean the tongue ; variety of courtship : What cannot a neat knave with a smooth tale Make a woman believe ? Farewell, lusty widow.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Shall this move me ? If all my royal kindred Lay in my way unto this marriage, I 'd make them my low footsteps : and even now, Even in this hate, as men in some great battles, By apprehending danger, have achievM Almost impossible actions (I have heard soldiers say so), So I through frights and threatenings will assay This dangerous venture. Let old wives report I wink'd and chose a husband.— Cariola, To thy known secrecy I have given up More than my life, — my fame.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Both shall be safe ; For I '11 conceal this secret from the world As warily as those that trade in poison Keep poison from their children.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Thy protestation Is ingenious and hearty : I believe it. Is Antonio come ?

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: He attends you.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Good dear soul, Leave me ; but place thyself behind the arras, Where thou mayst overhear us. Wish me good speed ; For I am going into a wilderness, Where I shall find nor path nor friendly clew To be my guide. I sent for you : sit down ; Take pen and ink, and write : are you ready?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: What did I say ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: That I should write somewhat.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, I remember. After these triumphs and this large expense It 's fit, like thrifty husbands, we inquire What 's laid up for to-morrow.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: So please your beauteous excellence. B

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Beauteous \ Indeed, I thank you : I look young for your sake ; You have ta'en my cares upon you.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I '11 fetch your grace The particulars of your revenue and expense.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, you are An upright treasurer : but you mistook ; For when I said I meant to make inquiry What 's laid up for to-morrow, I did mean What 's laid up yonder for me.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Where?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: In heaven. I am making my will (as 'tis fit princes should, In perfect memory), and, I pray, sir, tell me, Were not one better make it smiling, thus, Than in deep groans and terrible ghastly looks, As if the gifts we parted with procured That violent distraction ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: O, much better.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: If I had a husband now, this care were quit : But I intend to make you overseer. What good deed shall we first remember ? say.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Begin with that first good deed began i' the world After man's creation, the sacrament of marriage : I 'd have you first provide for a good husband ; Give him all.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: All !

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Yes, your excellent self.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: In a winding-sheet ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: In a couple.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Saint Winifred, that were a strange will !

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: 'Twere stranger if there were no will in you To marry again.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: What do you think of marriage ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I take 't, as those that deny purgatory, It locally contains or heaven or hell ; There 's no third place in 't.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: How do you affect it ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: My banishment, feeding my melancholy, Would often reason thus.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Pray, let 's hear it.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Say a man never marry, nor have children, What takes that from him ? only the bare name Of being a father, or the weak delight To see the little wanton ride a-cock-horse Upon a painted stick, or hear him chatter Like a taught starling.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Fie, fie, what 's all this ? One of your eyes is blood-shot ; use my ring to ' They say 'tis very sovereign : 'twas my \ wedding-ring, And I did vow never to part with it But to my second husband.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You have parted with it now.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Yes, to help your eye-sight.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You have made me stark blind.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: How?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: There is a saucy and ambitious devil Is dancing in this circle.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Remove him.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: How?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: There needs small conjuration, when your finger May do it : thus ; is it fit ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: What said you ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Sir, This goodly roof of yours is too low built ; I cannot stand upright in 't nor discourse, Without I raise it higher : raise yourself ; Or, if you please, my hand to help you : so.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Ambition, madam, is a great man's madness, That is not kept in chains and close-pent rooms, But in fair lightsome lodgings, and is girt With the wild noise of prattling visitants, Which makes it lunatic beyond all cure. Conceive not I am so stupid but I aim Whereto your favours tend : but he's a fool That, being a-cold, would thrust his hands i' the fire To warm them.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: So, now the ground 's broke, You may discover what a wealthy mine I make you lord of.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: O my unworthiness !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: You were ill to sell yourself : This darkening of your worth is not like that Which tradesmen use i' the city ; their false lights Are to rid bad wares off : and I must tell you, If you will know where breathes a cdmplete man (I speak it without flattery), turn your eyes, And progress through yourself.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Were there nor heaven nor hell, I should be honest : I have long serv'd virtue, And ne'er ta'en wages of her.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Now she pays it The misery of us that are born great ! We are forc'd to woo, because none dare woo us ; And as a tyrant doubles with his words, And fearfully equivocates, so we Are forc'd to express our violent passions A In riddles and in dreams, and leave the path Of simple virtue, which was never made To seem the thing it is not. Go, go brag You have left me heartless ; mine is in your bosom : I hope 'twill multiply love there. You do tremble : Make not your heart so dead a piece of flesh, To fear more than to love me. Sir, be confident : What is 't distracts you ? This is flesh and blood, sir; 'Tis not the figure cut in alabaster Kneels at my husband's tomb. Awake, awake, man I do here put off all vain ceremony, And only do appear to you a young widow That claims you for her husband, and, like a widow, I use but half a blush in 't.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Truth speak for me ; I will remain the constant sanctuary Of your good name.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I thank you, gentle love : And 'cause you shall not come to me in debt, Being now my steward, here upon your lips I sign your Quietus est. This you should have begg'd now : I have seen children oft eat sweetmeats thus, As fearful to devour them too soon.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: But for your brothers ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Do not think of them : All discord without this circumference Is only to be pitied, and not fear'd : Yet, should they know it, time will easily Scatter the tempest.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: These words should be mine, And all the parts you have spoke, if some part of it Would not have savour'd flattery.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Kneel.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Ha!

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Be not amaz'd ; this woman 's of my counsel : I have heard lawyers say, a contract in a chamber Per verba presenti is absolute marriage. Bless, heaven, this sacred gordian, which let violence Never untwine !

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: And may our sweet affections, like the spheres, Be still in motion !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Quickening, and make The like soft music !

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: That we may imitate the loving palms, Best emblem of a peaceful marriage, That never bore fruit, divided !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: What can the church force more ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: That fortune may not know an accident, Either of joy or sorrow, to divide Our fixed wishes !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: How can the church build faster ? We now are man and wife, and 'tis the church That must but echo this. — Maid, stand apart : I now am blind.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: What 's your conceit in this ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I would have you lead your fortune by the hand Unto your marriage-bed : (You speak in me this, for we now are one :) We '11 only lie, and talk together, and plot To appease my humorous kindred ; and if you please, Like the old tale in Alexander and Lodowick, Lay a naked sword between us, keep us chaste. O, let me shrowd my blushes in your bosom, Since 'tis the treasury of all my secrets !

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Whether the spirit of greatness or of woman Reign most in her, I know not ; but it shows A fearful madness : I owe her much of pity.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: You say you would fain be taken for an eminent courtier ?

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: 'Tis the very main of my ambition.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Let me see : you have a reasonable good face for't already, and your night-cap expresses your ears sufficient largely. I would have you learn to twirl the strings of your band with a good grace, and in a set speech, at the end of every sentence, to hum three or four times, or blow your nose till it smart again, to recover your memory. When you come to be a president in criminal causes, if you smile upon a prisoner, hang him ; but if you frown upon him and threaten him, let him be sure to 'scape the gallows.

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: I would be a very merry president.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Do not sup o' nights ; 'twill beget you an admirable wit.

speeches.speaker: CASTRUCCIO
speeches.text: Rather it would make me have a good stomach to quarrel ; for they say, your roaring boys eat meat seldom, and that makes them so valiant. But how shall I know whether the people take me for an eminent fellow ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I will teach a trick to know it : give out you lie a-dying, and if you hear the common people curse you, be sure you are taken for one of the prime night-caps. You come from painting now.

speeches.speaker: OLD LADY
speeches.text: From what ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Why, from your scurvy face-physic. To behold thee not painted inclines somewhat near a miracle : these in thy face here were deep ruts and foul sloughs the last progress. There was a lady inl France that, having had the small-pox, flayed the! skin off her face to make it more level ; and whereas before she looked like a nutmeg-grater, after shej resembled an abortive hedge-hog.

speeches.speaker: OLD LADY
speeches.text: Do you call this painting ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: No, no, but you call [it] careening of an old morphewed lady, to make her disembogue again: there 's rough-cast phrase to your plastic.

speeches.speaker: OLD LADY
speeches.text: It seems you are well acquainted with my closet.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: One would suspect it for a shop of witchcraft, to find in it the fat of serpents, spawn of snakes, Jews' spittle, and their young children's ordure ; and all these for the face. I would sooner eat a dead pigeon taken from the soles of the feet of one sick of the plague, than kiss one of you fasting. Here are two of you, whose sin of your youth is the very patrimony of the physician ; makes him renew his foot-cloth with the spring, and change his high-priced courtezan with the fall of the leaf. I do wonder you do not loathe yourselves. Observe my meditation now. What thing is in this outward form of man To be belov'd ? We account it ominous, If nature do produce a colt, or lamb, A fawn, or goat, in any limb resembling A man, and fly from 't as a prodigy : Man stands amaz'd to see his deformity In any other creature but himself. But in our own flesh though we bear diseases Which have their true names only ta'en from beasts, — As the most ulcerous wolf and swinish measle, — Though we are eaten up of lice and worms, And though continually we bear about us A rotten and dead body, we delight To hide it in rich tissue : all our fear, Nay, all our terror, is, lest our physician Should put us in the ground to be made sweet. — Your wife 's gone to Rome : you two couple, and get you to the wells at Lucca to recover your aches. I have other work on foot. I observe our duchess Is sick a-days, she pukes, her stomach seethes, The fins of her eye-lids look most teeming blue, She wanes i' the cheek, and waxes fat i' the flank, And, contrary to our Italian fashion, Wears a loose-bodied gown : there's somewhat in't. I have a trick may chance discover it, A pretty one ; I have bought some apricocks, The first our spring yields.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: And so long since married ? You amaze me.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Let me seal your lips for ever : For, did I think that anything but the air Could carry these words from you, I should wish You had no breath at all. — Now, sir, in your contemplation ? You are studying to become a great wise fellow.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, sir, the opinion of wisdom is a foul tetter that runs all over a man's body : if simplicity direct us to have no evil, it directs us to a happy being ; for the subtlest folly proceeds from the subtlest wisdom : let me be simply honest.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I do understand your inside.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Do you so ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Because you would not seem to appear to the world Puff 'd up with your preferment, you continue This out-of-fashion melancholy : leave it, leave it.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Give me leave to be honest in any phrase, in any compliment whatsoever. Shall I confess myself to you ? I look no higher than I can reach : they are the gods that must ride on winged horses. A lawyer's mule of a slow pace will both suit my disposition and business ; for, mark me, when a man's mind rides faster than his horse can gallop, they quickly both tire.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You would look up to heaven, but I think The devil, that rules i' the air, stands in your light.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, sir, you are lord of the ascendant, chief man with the duchess : a duke was your cousin-german removed. Say you were lineally descended from King Pepin, or he himself, what of this ? search the heads of the greatest rivers in the world, you shall find them but bubbles of water. Some would think the souls of princes were brought forth by some more weighty cause than those of meaner persons : they are deceived, there 's the same hand to them ; the like passions sway them ; the same reason that makes a vicar to go to law for a tithe-pig, and undo his neighbours, makes them spoil a whole province, and batter down goodly cities with the cannon.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Your arm, Antonio : do I not grow fat ? I am exceeding short-winded. — Bosola, I would have you, sir, provide for me a litter ; Such a one as the Duchess of Florence rode in.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: The duchess us'd one when she was great with child.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I think she did. — Come hither, mend my ruff : Here, when ? thou art such a tedious lady ; and Thy breath smells of lemon-pills : would thou hadst done ! Shall I swoon under thy ringers ? I am So troubled with the mother !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I fear too much.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I have heard you say that the French courtiers Wear their hats on 'fore the king.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I have seen it

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: In the presence ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Why should not we bring up that fashion ? 'Tis ceremony more than duty that consists In the removing of a piece of felt : Be you the example to the rest o' the court ; Put on your hat first.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You must pardon me : I have seen, in colder countries than in France, Nobles stand bare to the prince ; and the distinction Methought show'd reverently.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I have a present for your grace.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: For me, sir ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Apricocks, madam.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, sir, where are they ? I have heard of none to-year.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Good ; her colour rises.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Indeed, I thank you : they are wondrous fair ones. What an unskilful fellow is our gardener ! We shall have none this month.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Will not your grace pare them ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: No : they taste of musk, methinks; indeed they do.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I know not : yet I wish your grace had par'd ;em.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Why?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I forget to tell you, the knave gardener, Only to raise his profit by them the sooner, Did ripen them in horse-dung.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, you jest. — You shall judge : pray, taste one.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Indeed, madam, I do not love the fruit.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Sir, you are loth To rob us of our dainties : 'tis a delicate fruit ; They say they are restorative.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: 'Tis a pretty art, This grafting.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: 'Tis so ; bettering of nature.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: To make a pippin grow upon a crab, A damson on a black-thorn. — How greedily she eats them ! A whirlwind strike off these bawd farthingales I For, but for that and the loose-bodied gown, I should have discover'd apparently The young springal cutting a caper in her belly.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I thank you, Bosola : they were right good ones, If they do not make me sick.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: How now, madam !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: This green fruit and my stomach are not friends : How they swell me !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Nay, you are too much swell'd already.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, I am in an extreme cold sweat !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I am very sorry.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Lights to my chamber ! — O good Antonio, I fear I am undone !

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Lights there, lights !

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: O my most trusty Delio, we are lost ! I fear she 's fall'n in labour ; and there 's left No time for her remove.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Have you prepaid Those ladies to attend her ? and procur'd That politic safe conveyance for the midwife Your duchess plotted ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I have.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Make use, then, of this forc'd occasion : Give out that Bosola hath poison'd her With these apricocks ; that will give some colour For her keeping close.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Fie, fie, the physicians Will then flock to her.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: For that you may pretend She '11 use some prepaid antidote of her own, Lest the physicians should re-poison her.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I am lost in amazement : I know not what to think on't.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: So, so, there 's no question but her techiness and most vulturous eating of the apricocks are apparent signs of breeding. Now?

speeches.speaker: OLD LADY
speeches.text: I am in haste, sir.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: There was a young waiting-woman had a monstrous desire to see the glass-house

speeches.speaker: OLD LADY
speeches.text: Nay, pray, let me go.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: And it was only to know what strange instrument it was should swell up a glass to the fashion of a woman's belly.

speeches.speaker: OLD LADY
speeches.text: I will hear no more of the glass-house. You are still abusing women ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Who, I? no; only, by the way now and then, mention your frailties. The orange-tree bears ripe and green fruit and blossoms all together ; and some of you give entertainment for pure love, but more for more precious reward. The lusty spring smells well ; but drooping autumn tastes well. If we have the same golden showers that rained in the time of Jupiter the thunderer, you have the same Danaes still, to hold up their laps to receive them. Didst thou never study the mathematics ?

speeches.speaker: OLD LADY
speeches.text: What's that, sir?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Why, to know the trick how to make a many lines meet in one centre. Go, go, give your foster-daughters good counsel : tell them, that the devil takes delight to hang at a woman's girdle, like a false rusty watch, that she cannot discern how the time passes.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Shut up the court-gates.

speeches.speaker: RODERIGO
speeches.text: Why, sir ? what 's the danger ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Shut up the posterns presently, and call All the officers o} the court.

speeches.speaker: GRISOLAN
speeches.text: I shall instantly.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Who keeps the key o' the park-gate ?

speeches.speaker: RODERIGO
speeches.text: Forobosco.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Let him bring 't presently.

speeches.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
speeches.text: O, gentleman o' the court, the foulest treason !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: If that these apricocks should be poison'd now, Without my knowledge ?

speeches.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
speeches.text: There was taken even now a Switzer in the duchess' bed-chamber

speeches.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
speeches.text: A Switzer !

speeches.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
speeches.text: With a pistol in his great cod-piece.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Ha, ha, ha !

speeches.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
speeches.text: The cod-piece was the case for't.

speeches.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
speeches.text: There was a cunning traitor : who would have searched his cod-piece ?

speeches.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
speeches.text: True, if he had kept out of the ladies' chambers : and all the moulds of his buttons were leaden bullets.

speeches.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
speeches.text: O wicked cannibal ! a fire-lock in 's codpiece I

speeches.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
speeches.text: 'Twas a French plot, upon my life.

speeches.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
speeches.text: To see what the devil can do !

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: [Are] all the officers here ?

speeches.speaker: SERVANTS
speeches.text: We are.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Gentlemen, We have lost much plate you know ; and but this evening Jewels, to the value of four thousand ducats, Are missing in the duchess' cabinet. Are the gates shut ?

speeches.speaker: SERVANT
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: 'Tis the duchess' pleasure Each officer be lock'd into his chamber Till the sun-rising ; and to send the keys Of all their chests and of their outward doors Into her bed-chamber. She is very sick.

speeches.speaker: RODERIGO
speeches.text: At her pleasure.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: She entreats you take't not ill : the innocent Shall be the more approv'd by it.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Gentlemen o' the wood-yard, where 's your Switzer now?

speeches.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
speeches.text: By this hand, 'twas credibly reported by one o' the black guard.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: How fares it with the duchess ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: She'sexpos'd Unto the worst of torture, pain and fear.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Speak to her all happy comfort.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: How I do play the fool with mine own danger ! You are this night, dear friend, to post to Rome : My life lies in your service.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Do not doubt me.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: O, 'tis far from me : and yet fear presents me Somewhat that looks like danger.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Believe it, 'Tis but the shadow of your fear, no more : How superstitiously we mind our evils The throwing down salt, or crossing of a hare, Bleeding at nose, the stumbling of a horse, Or singing of a cricket, are of power To daunt whole man in us. Sir, fare you well : I wish you all the joys of a bless'd father ; And, for my faith, lay this unto your breast, — Old friends, like old swords, still are trusted best.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Sir, you are the happy father of a son : Your wife commends him to you.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Blessed comfort 1 — For heaven' sake, tend her well : I '11 presently Go set a figure for 's nativity.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Sure I did hear a woman shriek : list, ha ! And the sound came, if I receiv'd it right, From the duchess' lodgings. There's some stratagem In the confining all our courtiers To their several wards : I must have part of it ; My intelligence will freeze else. List, again It may be 'twas the melancholy bird, Best friend of silence and of solitariness, The owl, that screamed so. — Ha Antonio

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I heard some noise.— Who's there? what art thou? speak.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Antonio, put not your face nor body To such a forc'd expression of fear : I am Bosola, your friend.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Bosola! — This mole does undermine me. — Heard you not A noise even now ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: From whence ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: From the duchess' lodging.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Not I : did you ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I did, or else I dream'd.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Let 's walk towards it.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: No : it may be 'twas But the rising of the wind.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Very likely. Methinks 'tis very cold, and yet you sweat : You look wildly.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I have been setting a figure For the duchess' jewels.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Ah, and how falls your question ? Do you find it radical ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: What 's that to you ? 'Tis rather to be question'd what design, When all men were commanded to their lodgings, Makes you a night-walker.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: In sooth, I '11 tell you : Now all the court's asleep, I thought the devil Had least to do here ; I come to say my prayers ; And if it do offend you I do so, You are a fine courtier.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: This fellow will undo me. — You gave the duchess apricocks to-day : Pray heaven they were not poison'd

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Poison'd ! a Spanish fig For the imputation.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Traitors are ever confident Till they are discover'd. There were jewels stol'n too : In my conceit, none are to be suspected More than yourself.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: You are a false steward.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Saucy slave, I '11 pull thee up by the roots.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: May be the ruin will crush you to pieces.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You are an impudent snake indeed, sir : Are you scarce warm, and do you show your sting ? You libel well, sir.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: No, sir : copy it out, And I will set my hand to 't

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: My nose bleeds. One that were superstitious would count This ominous, when it merely comes by chance : Two letters, that are wrote here for my name, Are drown'd in blood Mere accident. — For you, sir, I '11 take order F the morn you shall be safe 'tis that must colour Her lying-in :— sir, this door you pass not : I do not hold it fit that you come near The duchess' lodgings, till you have quit yourself. — The great are like the base, nay, they are the same, When they seek shameful ways to avoid shame.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Antonio hereabout did drop a paper :— Some of your help, false friend : — O, here it is. What's here? a child's nativity calculated 1 ' The duchess was delivered of a son, *tween the hours twelve and one in the night. Anno Dom. 1504,'— that 's this year — * decimo nono Decembris] that's this night — ''taken according to the meridian of MalfiJ—\h&t 's our duchess : happy discovery ! — * The lord of the first house being combust in the ascendant, signifies short life ; and Mars being in a human sign, joined to the tail of the Dragon^ in the eighth house^ doth threaten a violent death. Cater a non scrutantur? Why, now 'tis most apparent ; this precise fellow Is the duchess' bawd : — I have it to my wish ! This is a parcel of intelligency Our courtiers were cas'd up for : it needs must follow That I must be committed on pretence Of poisoning her ; which I '11 endure, and laugh at. If one could find the father now ! but that Time will discover. Old Castruccio T the morning posts to Rome : by him I '11 send A letter that shall make her brothers' galls O'erflow their livers. This was a thrifty way. Though lust do mask in ne'er so strange disguise, She 's oft found witty, but is never wise.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Sit : thou art my best of wishes. Prithee, tell me What trick didst thou invent to come to Rome Without thy husband ?

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Why, my lord, I told him I came to visit an old anchorite Here for devotion.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Thou art a witty false one, — I mean, to him.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: You have prevail'd with me Beyond my strongest thoughts: I would not now Find you inconstant.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Do not put thyself To such a voluntary torture, which proceeds Out of your own guilt.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: How, my lord

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: You fear My constancy, because you have approv'd Those giddy and wild turnings in yourself.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Did you e'er find them ?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Sooth, generally for women, A man might strive to make glass malleable, Ere he should make them fixed.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: So, my lord.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: We had need go borrow that fantastic glass Invented by Galileo the Florentine To view another spacious world i' the moon, And look to find a constant woman there.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: This is very well, my lord.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Why do you weep ? Are tears your justification ? the self-same tears Will fall into your husband's bosom, lady, With a loud protestation that you love him Above the world. Come, I '11 love you wisely, That 's jealously ; since I am very certain You cannot make me cuckold.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: I '11 go home To my husband.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: You may thank me, lady, I have taken you off your melancholy perch, Bore you upon my fist, and show'd you game, And let you fly at it.— I pray thee, kiss me. — When thou wast with thy husband, thou wast watched Like a tame elephant : — still you are to thank me : — Thou hadst only kisses from him and high feeding ; But what delight was that ? 'twas just like one That hath a little fingering on the lute, Yet cannot tune it : — still you are to thank me.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: You told me of a piteous wound i' the heart, And a sick liver, when you woo'd me first, And spake like one in physic.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Who's that? Rest firm, for my affection to thee, Lightning moves slow to 't.

speeches.speaker: SERVANT
speeches.text: Madam, a gentleman, That 's comes post from Malfi, desires to see you.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Let him enter : I '11 withdraw.

speeches.speaker: SERVANT
speeches.text: He says Your husband, old Castruccio, is come to Rome, Most pitifully tir'd with riding post.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Signior Delio ! 'tis one of my old suitors.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I was bold to come and see you.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Sir, you are welcome.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Do you lie here ?

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Sure, your own experience Will satisfy you no : our Roman prelates Do not keep lodging for ladies.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Very well : I have brought you no commendations from your husband, For I know none by him.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: I hear he 's come to Rome. »

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I never knew man and beast, of a horse and a knight, So weary of each other : if he had had a good back, He would have undertook to have borne his horse, His breech was so pitifully sore.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Your laughter Is my pity.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Lady, I know not whether You want money, but I have brought you some.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: From my husband ?

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: No, from mine own allowance.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: I must hear the condition, ere I be bound to take it.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Look on 't, 'tis gold : hath it not a fine colour ?

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: I have a bird more beautiful.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Try the sound on 't.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: A lute-string far exceeds it : It hath no smell, like cassia or civet ; Nor is it physical, though some fond doctors Persuade us seethe 't in cullises. I '11 tell you, This is a creature bred by

speeches.speaker: SERVANT
speeches.text: Your husband's come, Hath deliver'd a letter to the Duke of Calabria That, to my thinking, hath put him out of his wits.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Sir, you hear : Pray, let me know your business and your suit As briefly as can be.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: With good speed : I would wish you, At such time as you are non-resident With your husband, my mistress.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Sir, I '11 go ask my husband if I shall, And straight return your answer.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Very fine ! Is this her wit, or honesty, that speaks thus ? I heard one say the duke was highly mov'd With a letter sent from Malfi. I do fear Antonio is betray'd : how fearfully Shows his ambition now ! unfortunate fortune ! They pass through whirl-pools, and deep woes do shun, Who the event weigh ere the action's done.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I have this night digg'd up a mandrake.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Say you ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: And I am grown mad with 't.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: What 's the prodigy ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Read there, — a sister damn'd : she 's loose i' the hilts ; Grown a notorious strumpet.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Speak lower.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Lower! Rogues do not whisper 't now, but seek to publish 't (As servants do the bounty of their lords) Aloud ; and with a covetous searching eye, To mark who note them. O, confusion seize her She hath had most cunning bawds to serve her turn, And more secure conveyances for lust Than towns of garrison for service.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Is't possible? Can this be certain ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Rhubarb, O, for rhubarb To purge this choler ! here 's the cursed day To prompt my memory ; and here 't shall stick Till of her bleeding heart I make a sponge To wipe it out.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Why do you make yourself So wild a tempest ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Would I could be one, That I might toss her palace 'bout her ears, Root up her goodly forests, blast her meads, And lay her general territory as waste As she hath done her honours.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Shall our blood, The royal blood of Arragon and Castile, Be thus attainted ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Apply desperate physic : We must not now use balsamum, but fire, The smarting cupping-glass, for that 's the mean To purge infected blood, such blood as hers. There is a kind of pity in mine eye, — I '11 give it to my handkercher ; and now 'tis here, I '11 bequeath this to her bastard.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: What to do ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Why, to make soft lint for his mother's wounds, When I have hew'd her to pieces.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Cursed creature ! Unequal nature, to place women's hearts So far upon the left side !

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Foolish men, That e'er will trust their honour in a bark Made of so slight weak bulrush as is woman, Apt every minute to sink it !

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Thus Ignorance, when it hath purchas'd honour, It cannot wield it.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Methinks I see her laughing, — Excellent hyena ! Talk to me somewhat quickly, Or my imagination will carry me To see her in the shameful act of sin.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: With whom ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Happily with some strong-thigh'd bargeman, Or one o' the wood-yard that can quoit the sledge Or toss the bar, or else some lovely squire That carries coals up to her privy lodgings.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: You fly beyond your reason.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Go to, mistress ! 'Tis not your whore's milk that shall quench my wild-fire, But your whore's blood.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: How idly shows this rage, which carries you, As men convey'd by witches through the air, On violent whirlwinds ! this intemperate noise Fitly resembles deaf men's shrill discourse, Who talk aloud, thinking all other men To have their imperfection.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Have not you My palsy ?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Yes, [but] I can be angry Without this rupture : there is not in nature A thing that makes man so deform'd, beastly, As doth intemperate anger. Chide yourself. You have divers men who never yet express'd Their strong desire of rest but by unrest, By vexing of themselves. Come, put yourself In tune. %

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: So I will only study to seem T^e thing I am not. I could kill her now, In you, or in myself; for I do think It is some sin in us heaven doth revenge By her.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Are you stark mad ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I would have their bodies Burnt in a coal-pit with the ventage stopp'd, That their curs'd smoke might not ascend to' heaven ; Or dip the sheets they lie in in pitch or sulphur, Wrap them in't, and then light them like a match ; Or else to-boil their bastard to a cullis, And give 't his lecherous father to renew The sin of his back.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: I '11 leave you.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Nay, I have done. I am confident, had I been damn'd in hell, D And should have heard of this, it would have put me Into a cold sweat. In, in ; I '11 go sleep. Till I know who leaps my sister, I '11 not stir : That known, I '11 find scorpions to string my whips, And fix her in a general eclipse.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Our noble friend, my most beloved Delio O, you have been a stranger long at court : Came you along with the Lord Ferdinand ?

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I did, sir : and how fares your noble duchess ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Right fortunately well : she 's an excellent Feeder of pedigrees ; since you last saw her, She hath had two children more, a son and daughter.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Methinks 'twas yesterday : let me but wink, And not behold your face, which to mine eye Is somewhat leaner, verily I should dream It were within this half hour.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You have not been in law, friend Delio, Nor in prison, nor a suitor at the court, Norjbegg'd the reversion of some great man's place, Nor troubled with an old wife, which doth make Your time so insensibly hasten.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Pray, sir, tell me, Hath not this news arriv'd yet to the ear Of the lord cardinal ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I fear it hath : The Lord Ferdinand, that 's newly come to court, Doth bear himself right dangerously.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Pray, why ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: He is so quiet that he seems to sleep The tempest out, as dormice do in winter : Those houses that are haunted are most still Till the devil be up.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: What say the common people ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: The common rabble do directly say She is a strumpet.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: And your graver heads Which would be politic, what censure they?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: They do observe I grow to infinite purchase, The left hand way ; and all suppose the duchess Would amend it, if she could ; for, say they, Great princes, though they grudge their officers Should have such large and unconfined means To get wealth under them, will not complain, Lest thereby they should make them odious . Unto the people : for other obligation Of love or marriage between her and me They never dream of.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: The Lord Ferdinand Is going to bed.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I '11 instantly to bed, For I am weary. — I am to bespeak A husband for you.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: For me, sir ! pray, who is 't ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: The great Count Malatesti.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Fie upon him ! A count ! he 's a mere stick of sugar-candy ; You may look quite through him. When I choose A husband, I will marry for your honour.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You shall do well in 't. — How is 't, worthy Antonio?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: But, sir, I am to have private conference with you About a scandalous report is spread Touching mine honour.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Let me be ever deaf to 't : One of Pasquil's paper-bullets, court-calumny, A pestilent air, which princes' palaces Are seldom purg'd of. Yet say that it were true, I pour it in your bosom, my fix'd love Would strongly excuse, extenuate, nay, deny Faults, were they apparent in you. Go, be safe In your own innocency.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O bless'd comfort This deadly air is purg'd.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Her guilt treads on Hot-burning coulters. Now, Bosola, How thrives our intelligence ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Sir, uncertainly : 'Tis rumour'd she hath had three bastards, but By whom we may go read i3 the stars.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Why, some Hold opinion all things are written there.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yes, if we could find spectacles to read them. I do suspect there hath been some sorcery Us'd on the duchess.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Sorcery ! to what purpose ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: To make her dote on some desertless fellow She shames to acknowledge.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Can your faith give way To think there 's power in potions or in charms, To make us love whether we will or no ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Most certainly.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Away ! these are mere gulleries, horrid things, I Invented by some cheating mountebanks l To abuse us. Do you think that herbs or charms I Can force the will ? Some trials have been made In this foolish practice, but the ingredients I Were lenitive poisons, such as are of force To make the patient mad ; and straight the witch Swears by equivocation they are in love. The witch-craft lies in her rank blood. This night I will force confession from her. You told me You had got, within these two days, a false key Into her bed-chamber.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I have.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: As I would wish.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: What do you intend to do ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Can you guess ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: No.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Do not ask, then : He that can compass me, and know my drifts, May say he hath put a girdle 'bout the world, And sounded all her quick-sands.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I do not Think so.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: What do you think, then, pray ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: That you are Your own chronicle too much, and grossly Flatter yourself.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Give me thy hand ; I thank thee : I never gave pension but to flatterers, Till I entertained thee. Farewell. That friend a great man's ruin strongly checks, Who rails into his belief all his defects.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Bring me the casket hither, and the glass. — You get no lodging here to-night, my lord.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Indeed, I must persuade one.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Very good : I hope in time 'twill grow into a custom, That noblemen shall come with cap and knee To purchase a night's lodging of their wives.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I must lie here.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Must ! you are a lord of mis-rule.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Indeed, my rule is only in the night.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: To what use will you put me ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: We'll sleep together.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Alas, What pleasure can two lovers find in sleep !

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: My lord, I lie with her often ; and I know She '11 much disquiet you.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: See, you are complain'd of.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: For she 's the sprawling'st bedfellow.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I shall like her the better for that.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Sir, shall I ask you a question f

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Ay, pray thee, Cariola.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Wherefore still, when you lie with my lady, Do you rise so early ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Labouring men Count the clock oftenest, Cariola, Are glad when their task 's ended.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I '11 stop your mouth.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Nay, that 's but one ; Venus had two soft doves To draw her chariot ; I must have another. — When wilt thou marry, Cariola ?

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Never, my lord.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: O, fie upon this single life ! forgo it. We read how Daphne, for her peevish flight, Became a fruitless bay-tree ; Syrinx turn'd To the pale empty reed ; Anaxarete Was frozen into marble : whereas those Which married, or prov'd kind unto their friends, Were by a gracious influence transhap'd Into the olive, pomegranate, mulberry, Became flowers, precious stones, or eminent stars.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: This is a vain poetry : but I pray you, tell me, If there were propos'd me, wisdom, riches, and beauty, In three several young men, which should I choose?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: 'Tis a hard question : this was Paris' case, And he was blind in't, and there was a great cause ; For how was 't possible he could judge right, Having three amorous goddesses in view, And they stark naked ? 'twas a motion Were able to benight the apprehension Of the severest counsellor of Europe. Now I look on both your faces so well form'd, It puts me in mind of a question I would ask.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: What is 't?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I do wonder why hard-favour'd ladies, For the most part, keep worse-favour'd waiting-women To attend them, and cannot endure fair ones.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, that 's soon answer'd. Did you ever in your life know an ill painter Desire to have his dwelling next door to the shop Of an excellent picture-maker ? 'twould disgrace His face-making, and undo him. I prithee, When were we so merry ? — My hair tangles.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Pray thee, Cariola, let 's steal forth the room, And let her talk to herself : I have divers times Serv'd her the like, when she hath chaf d extremely. I love to see her angry. Softly, Cariola.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Doth not the colour of my hair 'gin to change ? When I wax gray, I shall have all the court Powder their hair with arras, to be like me. You have cause to love me ; I enter'd you into my heart Before you would vouchsafe to call for the keys. We shall one day have my brothers take you napping : Methinks his presence, being now in court, Should make you keep your own bed ; but you'll say Love mix'd with fear is sweetest. I '11 assure you, You shall get no more children till my brothers Consent to be your gossips. H ave you lost your tongue? 'Tis welcome : For know, whether I am doom'd to live or die, I can do both like a prince.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Die, then, quickly ! Virtue, where art thou hid ? what hideous thing Is it that doth eclipse thee ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Pray, sir, hear me.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Or is it true thou art but a bare name, And no essential thing ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Sir

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Do not speak,

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: No, sir : I will plant my soul in mine ears, to hear you.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: O most imperfect light of human reason, That mak'st us so unhappy to foresee What we can least prevent ! Pursue thy wishes, And glory in them : there 's in shame no comfort But to be past all bounds and sense of shame.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I pray, sir, hear me : I am married.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: So !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Happily, not to your liking : but for that, Alas, your shears do come untimely now To clip the bird's wings that 's already flown ! Will you see my husband ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Yes, if I could change Eyes with a basilisk.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Sure, you came hither By his confederacy.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: The howling of a wolf Is music to thee, screech-owl : prithee, peace.— Whate'er thou art that hast enjoyM my sister, For I am sure thou hear'st me, for thine own sake Let me not know thee. I came hither prepaid To work thy discovery ; yet am now persuaded It would beget such violent effects As would damn us both. I would not for ten millions I had beheld thee : therefore use all means I never may have knowledge of thy name ; Enjoy thy lust still, and a wretched life, On that condition. — And for thee, vile woman, If thou do wish thy lecher may grow old In thy embracements, I would have thee build Such a room for him as our anchorites To holier use inhabit. Let not the sun Shine on him till he 's dead ; let dogs and monkeys Only converse with him, and such dumb things To whom nature denies use to sound his name ; Do not keep a paraquito, lest she learn it ; If thou do love him, cut out thine own tongue, Lest it bewray him.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Why might not I marry ? I have not gone about in this to create Any new world or custom.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Thou art undone ; And thou hast ta'en that massy sheet of lead That hid thy husband's bones, and folded it About my heart.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Mine bleeds for 't

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Thine ! thy heart ! What should I name 't unless a hollow bullet Fill'd with unquenchable wild-fire ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: You are in this Too strict ; and were you not my princely brother, I would say, too wilful : my reputation Is safe.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Dost thou know what reputation is ? I '11 tell thee, — to small purpose, since the instruction Comes now too late. Upon a time Reputation, Love, and Death, Would travel o'er the world ; and it was concluded That they should part, and take three several ways. Death told them, they should find him in great battles, Or cities plagu'd with plagues : Love gives them counsel To inquire for him 'mongst unambitious shepherds, Where dowries were not talk'd of, and sometimes 'Mongst quiet kindred that had nothing left By their dead parents : ' Stay,' quoth Reputation, ' Do not forsake me ; for it is my nature, If once I part from any man I meet, 1 am never found again.' And so for you : You have shook hands with Reputation, And made him invisible. So, fare you well : I will never see you more.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Why should only I, Of all the other princes of the world, Be cas'd up, like a holy relic ? I have youth And a little beauty.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: So you have some virgins That are witches. I will never see thee more.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: You saw this apparition ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Yes : we are Betrayed. How came he hither ? I should turn This to thee, for that.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Pray, sir, do ; and when That you have cleft my heart, you shall read there Mine innocence.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: That gallery gave him entrance.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I would this terrible thing would come again, That, standing on my guard, I might relate My warrantable love. — Ha ! what means this ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: He left this with me.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: And it seems did wish You would use it on yourself.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: His action Seem'd to intend so much.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: This hath a handle to 't, As well as a point : turn it towards him, And so fasten the keen edge in his rank gall. How now 1 who knocks ? more earthquakes ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I stand As if a mine beneath my feet were ready To be blown up.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: 'Tis Bosola.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Awayl O misery ! methinks unjust actions Should wear these masks and curtains, and not we. You must instantly part hence : I have fashion'd it already.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: The duke your brother is ta'en up in a whirlwind ; Hath took horse, and 's rid post to Rome.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: So late ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: He told me, as he mounted into the saddle, You were undone.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Indeed, I am very near it.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: What 's the matter ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Antonio, the master of our household, Hath dealt so falsely with me in 's accounts : My brother stood engag'd with me for money Ta'en up of certain Neapolitan Jews, And Antonio lets the bonds be forfeit.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Strange \-\AsideI\ This is cunning.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: And hereupon My brother's bills at Naples are protested Against. — Call up our officers.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I shall.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: The place that you must fly to is Ancona : Hire a house there ; I '11 send after you My treasure and my jewels. Our weak safety Runs upon enginous wheels : short syllables Must stand for periods. I must now accuse you Of such a feigned crime as Tasso calls Magnanima menzogna, a noble lie, 'Cause it must shield our honours. — Hark ! they are coming.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Will your grace hear me ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I have got well by you ; you have yielded me A million of loss : I am like to inherit The people's curses for your stewardship. You had the trick in audit-time to be sick, Till I had signed your quietus ; and that cur'd you Without help of the doctor.— Gentlemen, I would have this man be an example to you all ; So shall you hold my favour ; I pray, let him ; For h'as done that, alas, you would not think of, And, because I intend to be rid of him, I mean not to publish. — Use your fortune elsewhere.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I am strongly arm'd to brook my overthrow, As commonly men bear with a hard year : I will not blame the cause on 't ; but do think The necessity of my malevolent star Procures this, not her humour. O, the inconstant And rotten ground of service ! you may see, 'Tis even like him, that in a winter night, Takes a long slumber o'er a dying fire, A-loth to part from 't ; yet parts thence as cold As when he first sat down.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: We do confiscate, Towards the satisfying of your accounts, All that you have.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I am all yours ; and 'tis very fit All mine should be so.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: So, sir, you have your pass.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
