speeches.text: You may see, gentlemen, what 'tis to serve A prince with body and soul.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Here 's an example for extortion : what moisture is drawn out of the sea, when foul weather comes, pours down, and runs into the sea again. E

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I would know what are your opinions Of this Antonio.

speeches.speaker: SECOND OFFICER
speeches.text: He could not abide to see a pig's head gaping : I thought your grace would find him a Jew.

speeches.speaker: THIRD OFFICER
speeches.text: I would you had been his officer, for your own sake.

speeches.speaker: FOURTH OFFICER
speeches.text: You would have had more money.

speeches.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
speeches.text: He stopped his ears with black wool, and to those came to him for money said he was thick of hearing.

speeches.speaker: SECOND OFFICER
speeches.text: Some said he was an hermaphrodite, for he could not abide a woman.

speeches.speaker: FOURTH OFFICER
speeches.text: How scurvy proud he would look when the treasury was full ! Well, let him go.

speeches.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
speeches.text: Yes, and the chippings of the buttery fly after him, to scour his gold chain.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Leave us. What do you think of these ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: That these are rogues that in 's prosperity, But to have waited on his fortune, could have wish'd His dirty stirrup riveted through their noses, And folio w'd after 's mule, like a bear in a ring ; Would have prostituted their daughters to his lust , Made their first-born intelligencers ; thought none happy But such as were born under his blest planet, And wore his livery : and do these lice drop oft now? Well, never look to have the like again : He hath left a sort of flattering rogues behind him ; Their doom must follow. Princes pay flatterers In their own money : flatterers dissemble their vices, And they dissemble their lies ; that 's justice. Alas, poor gentleman !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Poor ! he hath amply fill'd his coffers.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Sure, he was too honest. Pluto, the god of riches, When he 's sent by Jupiter to any man, He goes limping, to signify that wealth That comes on God's name comes slowly ; but when he's sent On the devil's errand, he rides post and comes in by scuttles. Let me show you what a most unvalued jewel You have in a wanton humour thrown away, To bless the man shall find him. He was an excellent Courtier and most faithful ; a soldier that thought it As beastly to know his own value too little As devilish to acknowledge it too much. Both his virtue and form deserv'd a far better fortune: His discourse rather delighted to judge itself than show itself : His breast was filled with all perfection, And yet it seemed a private whispering-room, It made so little noise oft.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: But he was basely descended.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Will you make yourself a mercenary herald, Rather to examine men's pedigrees than virtues ? You shall want him : For know an honest statesman to a prince Is like a cedar planted by a spring ; The spring bathes the tree's root, the grateful tree Rewards it with his shadow : you have not done so. I would sooner swim to the Bennoothes on Two politicians' rotten bladders, tied Together with an intelligencer's heart-string, Than depend on so changeable a prince's favour. Fare thee well, Antonio ! since the malice of the world Would needs down with thee, it cannot be said yet That any ill happen'd unto thee, considering thy fall Was accompanied with virtue.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, you render me excellent music !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Say you ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: This good one that you speak of is my husband.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Do I not dream? can this ambitious age Have so much goodness in 't as to prefer A man merely for worth, without these shadows Of wealth and painted honours ? possible ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I have had three children by him.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Fortunate lady ! For you have made your private nuptial bed The humble and fair seminary of peace. No question but many an unbenefic'd scholar Shall pray for you for this deed, and rejoice That some preferment in the world can yet Arise from merit. The virgins of your land That have no dowries shall hope your example Will raise them to rich husbands. Should-'you want Soldiers, 'twould make the very Turks and Moors Turn Christians, and serve you for this act. Last, the neglected poets of your time, In honour of this trophy of a man, Rais'd by that curious engine, your white hand, Shall thank you, in your grave, for 't ; and make that More reverend than all the cabinets Of living princes. For Antonio, His fame shall likewise flow from many a pen, When heralds shall want coats to sell to men.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: As I taste comfort in this friendly speech, So would I find concealment.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, the secret of my prince. Which I will wear on the inside of my heart !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: You shall take charge of all my coin and jewels, And follow him ; for he retires himself To Ancona.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: So.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Whither, within few days, I mean to follow thee.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Let me think : I would wish your grace to feign a pilgrimage To our Lady of Loretto, scarce seven leagues From fair Ancona ; so may you depart Your country with more honour, and your flight Will seem a princely progress, retaining Your usual train about you.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Sir, your direction Shall lead me by the hand.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: In my opinion, She were better progress to the baths at Lucca, Or go visit the Spa In Germany ; for, if you will believe me, I do not like this jesting with religion, This feigned pilgrimage.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Thou art a superstitious fool : Prepare us instantly for our departure. Past sorrows, let us moderately lament them, For those to come, seek wisely to prevent them.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: A politician is the devil's quilted anvil ; He fashions all sins on him, and the blows Are never heard : he may work in a lady's chamber, As here for proof. What rests but I reveal All to my lord ? O, this base quality Of intelligencer ! why, every quality i' the world Prefers but gain or commendation : Now, for this act I am certain to be rais'd, And men that paint weeds to the life are prais'd.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Must we turn soldier, then ?

speeches.speaker: MALATESTI
speeches.text: The emperor, Hearing your worth that way, ere you attam'd This reverend garment, joins you in commission WiththerightfortunatesoldiertheMarquisofPescara, And the famous Lannoy.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: He that had the honour Of taking the French king prisoner ?

speeches.speaker: MALATESTI
speeches.text: The same. Here 's a plot drawn for a new fortification At Naples.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: This great Count Malatesti, T perceive, Hath got employment ?

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: No employment, my lord ; A marginal note in the muster-book, that he is A voluntary lord.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: He's no soldier.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: He has worn gun-powder in's hollow tooth for the tooth-ache.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: He comes to the leaguer with a full intent To eat fresh beef and garlic, means to stay Till the scent be gone, and straight return to court.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: He hath read all the late service As the City-Chronicle relates it ; And keeps two pewterers going, only to express Battles in model.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: Then he'll fight by the book.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: By the almanac, I think, To choose good days and shun the critical ; That 's his mistress' scarf.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: Yes, he protests He would do much for that taffeta.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I think he would run away from a battle, To save it from taking prisoner.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: He is horribly afraid Gun-powder will spoil the perfume on 'U

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I saw a Dutchman break his pate once For calling him pot-gun ; he made his head Have a bore in 't like a musket.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: I would he had made a touch-hole to 't. He is indeed a guarded sumpter-cloth, Only for the remove of the court.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Bosola arriv'd ! what should be the business ? Some falling-out amongst the cardinals. These factions amongst great men, they are like Foxes, when their heads are divided, They carry fire in their tails, and all the country About them goes to wreck for't.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: What 's that Bosola ?

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I knew him in Padua, — a fantastical scholar, like such who study to know how many knots was in \ Hercules' club, of what colour Achilles' beard was, or whether Hector were not troubled with the tooth-ache. He hath studied himself half blear-eyed to know the true symmetry of Caesar's nose by a shoeing-horn ; and this he did to gain the name of a speculative man.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Mark Prince Ferdinand : A very salamander lives in 's eye, To mock the eager violence of fire.

speeches.speaker: SILVIO
speeches.text: That cardinal hath made more bad faces with his oppression than ever Michael Angelo made good ones : he lifts up 's nose, like a foul porpoise before a storm.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: The Lord Ferdinand laughs.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Like a deadly cannon That lightens ere it smokes.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: These are your true pangs of death, The pangs of life, that struggle with great statesmen.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: In such a deformed silence witches whisper their charms.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Doth she make religion her riding-hood To keep her from the sun and tempest ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: That, That damns her. Methinks her fault and beauty, Blended together, show like leprosy, The whiter, the fouler. I make it a question Whether her beggarly brats were ever christen'd.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: I will instantly solicit the state of Ancona To have them banish'd.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You are for Loretto : I shall not be at your ceremony ; fare you well. — Write to the Duke of Malfi, my young nephew She had by her first husband, and acquaint him With 's mother's honesty.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I will.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Antonio A slave that only smelFd of ink and counters, And never in 's life look'd like afgentleman, But in the audit-time. — Go, go presently, Draw me out an hundred and fifty of our horse, And meet me at the foot-bridge.

speeches.speaker: FIRST PILGRIM
speeches.text: I have not seen a goodlier shrine than this ; Yet I have visited many.

speeches.speaker: SECOND PILGRIM
speeches.text: The Cardinal of Arragon Is this day to resign his cardinal's hat : His sister duchess likewise is arriv'd To pay her vow of pilgrimage. I expect A noble ceremony.

speeches.speaker: FIRST PILGRIM
speeches.text: No question. — They come.

speeches.speaker: CHURCHMEN
speeches.text: Arms and honours deck thy story, To thy fame's eternal glory ! Adverse fortune ever fly thee ; No disastrous fete come nigh thee ! I alone will sing thy praises, Whom to honour virtue raises, And thy study, that divine is, Bent to martial discipline is, Lay aside all those robes lie by thee ; Crown thy arts with arms, they '11 beautify thee. O worthy of worthiest name, adorn'd in this manner, Lead bravely thy forces on under war's warlike banner ! O, mayst thou prove fortunate in all martial courses ! Guide thou still by skill in art and forces Victory attend thee nigh, whilst fame sings loud thy powers ; Triumphant conquest crown thy head, and blessings pour down showers !

speeches.speaker: FIRST PILGRIM
speeches.text: Here 's a strange turn of state 1 who would have thought So great a lady would have match'd herself Unto so mean a person ? yet the cardinal Bears himself much too cruel.

speeches.speaker: SECOND PILGRIM
speeches.text: They are banish'd.

speeches.speaker: FIRST PILGRIM
speeches.text: But I would ask what power hath this state Of Ancona to determine of a free prince ?

speeches.speaker: SECOND PILGRIM
speeches.text: They are a free state, sir, and her brother show'd How that the Pope, fore-hearing of her looseness, Hath seiz'd into the protection of the church The dukedom which she held as dowager.

speeches.speaker: FIRST PILGRIM
speeches.text: But by what justice ?

speeches.speaker: SECOND PILGRIM
speeches.text: Sure, I think by none, Only her brother's instigation.

speeches.speaker: FIRST PILGRIM
speeches.text: What was it with such violence he took Off from her finger ?

speeches.speaker: SECOND PILGRIM
speeches.text: 'Twas her wedding-ring ; Which he vow'd shortly he would sacrifice To his revenge.

speeches.speaker: FIRST PILGRIM
speeches.text: Alas, Antonio ! If that a man be thrust into a well, No matter who sets hand to 't, his own weight Will bring him sooner to the bottom. Come, let 's hence. Fortune makes this conclusion general, All things do help the unhappy man to fall.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Banish'd Ancona !

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Yes, you see what power Lightens in great men's breath.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Is all our train Shrunk to this poor remainder ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: These poor men, Which have got little in your service, vow To take your fortune : but your wiser buntings, Now they are fledg'd, are gone.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: They have done wisely. This puts me in mind of death : physicians thus, With their hands full of money, use to give o'er Their patients.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Right the fashion of the world : From decay'd fortunes every flatterer shrinks ; Men cease to build where the foundation sinks.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I had a very strange dream to-night.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: What was 't?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Methought I wore my coronet of state, And on a sudden all the diamonds Were changed to pearls.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: My interpretation Is, you'll weep shortly ; for to me the pearls Do signify your tears.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: The birds that live i' the field On the wild benefit of nature live Happier than we ; for they may choose their mates, And carol their sweet pleasures to the spring.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: You are happily o'erta'en.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: From my brother ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yes, from the Lord Ferdinand your brother All love and safety.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Thou dost blanch mischief, Would'st make it white. See, see, like to calm weather At sea before a tempest, false hearts speak fair To those they intend most mischief. ' Send Antonio to me; I want his head in a business* A politic equivocation ! He doth not want your counsel, but your head ; That is, he cannot sleep till you be dead. And here 's another pitfall that 's strew* d o'er With roses ; mark it, 'tis a cunning one : 1 / stand engaged for your husband for several debts at Naples: let not that trouble him; I had rather have his heart than his money ' : — And I believe so too.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: What do you believe ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: That he so much distrusts my husband's love, He will by no means believe his heart is with him Until he see it : the devil is not cunning enough To circumvent us in riddles.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Will you reject that noble and free league Of amity and love which I present you ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Their league is like that of some politic kings, Only to make themselves of strength and power To be our after-ruin ; tell them so.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: And what from you ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Thus tell him ; I will not come.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: And what of this ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: My brothers have dispers'd Bloodhounds abroad; which till I hear are muzzled, No truce, though hatch'd with ne'er such politic skill, Is safe, that hangs upon our enemies' will. I '11 not come at them.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: This proclaims your breeding : Every small thing draws a base mind to fear, As the adamant draws iron. Fare you well, sir : You shall shortly hear from 's.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I suspect some ambush : Therefore by all my love I do conjure you To take your eldest son, and fly towards Milan. Let us not venture all this poor remainder In one unlucky bottom.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You counsel safely. Best of my life, farewell, since we must part : Heaven hath a hand in 't ; but no otherwise Than as some curious artist takes in sunder A clock or watch, when it is out of frame, To bring 't in better order.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I know not which is best, To see you dead, or part with you.— Farewell, boy : Thou art happy that thou hast not understanding To know thy misery ; for all our wit And reading brings us to a truer sense Of sorrow. — In the eternal church, sir, I do hope we shall not part thus.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: O, be of comfort ! Make patience a noble fortitude, And think not how unkindly we are us'd : Man, like to cassia, is prov'd best, being bruis'd.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Must I, like to a slave-born Russian, Account it praise to suffer tyranny ? And yet, O heaven, thy heavy hand is in 't ! I have seen my little boy oft scourge his top, And compared myself to 't : naught made me e'er Go right but heaven's scourge-stick.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Do not weep : Heaven fashion'd us of nothing ; and we strive To bring ourselves to nothing. — Farewell, Cariola, And thy sweet armful.— If I do never see thee more, Be a good mother to your little ones, And save them from the tiger : fare you well.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Let me look upon you once more, for that speech Came from a dying father : your kiss is colder Than that I have seen an holy anchorite Give to a dead man's skull.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: My heart is turn'd to a heavy lump of lead, With which I sound my danger : fare you well.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: My laurel is all wither'd.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Look, madam, what a troop of armed men Make toward us !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, they are very welcome : When Fortune's wheel is over-charg'd with princes, The weight makes it move swift : I would have my ruin Be sudden. I am your adventure, am I not ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: You are : you must see your husband no more.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: What devil art thou that counterfeit'st heaven's thunder ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Is that terrible ? I would have you tell me whether p Is that note worse that frights the silly birds Out of the corn, or that which doth allure them To the nets? you have hearken'd to the last too much.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O misery ! like to a rusty o'erchargM cannon, Shall I never fly in pieces ? — Come, to what prison ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: To none.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Whither, then ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: To your palace.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I have heard That Charon's boat serves to convey all o'er The dismal lake, but brings none back again.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Your brothers mean you safety and pity.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Pity! With such a pity men preserve alive Pheasants and quails, when they are not fat enough To be eaten.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: These are your children ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Can they prattle ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: No : But I intend, since they were born accurs'd, Curses shall be their first language.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Fie, madam ! Forget this base, low fellow

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Were I a man, I 'd beat that counterfeit face into thy other.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: One of no birth.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Say that he was born mean, Man is most happy when 's own actions Be arguments and examples of his virtue.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: A barren, beggarly virtue.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I prithee, who is greatest ? can you tell ? Sad tales befit my woe : I '11 tell you one. A salmon, as she swam unto the sea, Met with a dog-fish, who encounters her With this rough language ; ' Why art thou so bold To mix thyself with our high state of floods, Being no eminent courtier, but one That for the calmest and fresh time o' the year Dost live in shallow rivers, rank'st thyself With silly smelts and shrimps ? and darest thou Pass by our dog-ship without reverence ? ' * O,' quoth the salmon, * sister, be at peace : Thank Jupiter we both have pass'd the net ! Our value never can be truly known, Till in the fisher's basket we be shown : V the market then my price may be the higher, Even when I am nearest to the cook and fire.' So to great men the moral may be stretch'd ; Men oftare valu'd high, when they 're most wretch'd. — But come, whither you please. I am arm'd 'gainst misery; Bent to all sways of the oppressor's will : There 's no deep valley but near some great hill.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: How doth our sister duchess bear herself In her imprisonment ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Nobly : I '11 describe her. She 's sad as one long us'd to \ and she seems Rather to welcome the end of misery Than shun it ; a behaviour so noble As gives a majesty to adversity : You may discern the shape of loveliness More perfect in her tears than in her smiles : She will muse for hours together ; and her silence, Methinks, expresseth more than if she spake.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Her melancholy seems to be fortified With a strange disdain.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: 'Tis so ; and this restraint, Like English mastives that grow fierce with tying, Makes her too passionately apprehend Those pleasures she 's kept from.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Curse upon her ! I will no longer study in the book Of another's heart Inform her what I told you.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: All comfort to your grace !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I will have none. Pray thee, why dost thou wrap thy poison'd pills In gold and sugar ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Your elder brother, the Lord Ferdinand, Is come to visit you, and sends you word, 'Cause once he rashly made a solemn vow Never to see you more, he comes i' the night ; And prays you gently neither torch nor taper Shine in your chamber : he will kiss your hand, And reconcile himself ; but for his vow He dares not see you.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: At his pleasure. — Take hence the lights.— He 's come.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Where are you ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Here, sir.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: This darkness suits you well.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I would ask you pardon.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You have it ; For I account it the honorabl'st revenge, Where I may kill, to pardon. — Where are your cubs?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Whom?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Call them your children ; For though our national law distinguish bastards From true legitimate issue, compassionate nature Makes them all equal.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Do you visit me for this ? You violate a sacrament o' the church Shall make you howl in hell for 't.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: It had been well, Could you have liv'd thus always ; for, indeed, You were too much i' the light : — but no more ; I come to seal my peace with you. Here 's a hand To which you have vow'd much love; the ring upon 't You gave.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I affectionately kiss it.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Pray, do, and bury the print of it in your heart. I will leave this ring with you for a love-token ; And the hand as sure as the ring ; and do not doubt But you shall have the heart too : when you need a friend, Send it to him that ow'd it ; you shall see Whether he can aid you.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: You are very cold : I fear you are not well after your travel.— Ha ! lights ! O, horrible !

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Let her have lights enough.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: What witchcraft doth he practise, that he hath left A dead man's hand here.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Look you, here 's the piece from which 'twas ta'en. He doth present you this sad spectacle, That, now you know directly they are dead, Hereafter you may wisely cease to grieve For that which cannot be recovered.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: There is not between heaven and earth one wish I stay for after this : it wastes me more Than were 't my picture, fashion'd out of wax, Stuck with a magical needle, and then buried In some foul dunghill ; and yond 's an excellent property For a tyrant, which I would account mercy.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: What 's that ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: If they would bind me to that lifeless trunk, And let me freeze to death.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Come, you must live.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: That 's the greatest torture souls feel in hell, In hell, that they must live, and cannot die. Portia, I '11 new kindle thy coals again, And revive the rare and almost dead example Of a loving wife.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, fie ! despair ? remember You are a Christian.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: The church enjoins fasting : I ;11 starve myself to death.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Leave this vain sorrow. Things being at the worst begin to mend : the bee When he hath shot his sting into your hand, May then play with your eye-lid.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Good comfortable fellow, Persuade a wretch that 's broke upon the wheel To have all his bones new set ; entreat him live To be executed again. Who must despatch me ? I account this world a tedious theatre, For I do play a part in 't 'gainst my will.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Come, be of comfort ; I will save your life.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Indeed, I have not leisure to tend So small a business.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Now, by my life, I pity you.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Thou art a fool, then, To waste thy pity on a thing so wretched As cannot pity itself. I am full of daggers. Puff, let me blow these vipers from me. no What are you ?

speeches.speaker: SERVANT
speeches.text: One that wishes you long life.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I would thou wert hang'd for the horrible curse Thou hast given me : I shall shortly grow one Of the miracles of pity. I '11 go pray ;— - No, I '11 go curse.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, fie !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I could curse the stars.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, fearful !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: And those three smiling seasons of the year Into a Russian winter : nay, the world To its first chaos.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Look you, the stars shine still.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, but you must Remember, my curse hath a great way to go. — Plagues, that make lanes through largest families, Consume them !—

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Fie, lady I

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Let them, like tyrants, Never be remember'd but for the ill they have done ; Let all the zealous prayers of mortified Churchmen forget them ! —

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, uncharitable !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Let heaven a little while cease crowning martyrs, To punish them ! — Go, howl them this, and say, I long to bleed : It is some mercy when men kill with speed.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Excellent, as I would wish ; she's plagu'd in art : These presentations are but fram'd in wax By the curious master in that quality, Vincentio Lauriola, and she takes them For true substantial bodies.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Why do you do this ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: To bring her to despair.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Faith, end here, And go no farther in your cruelty : Send her a penitential garment to put on Next to her delicate skin, and furnish her With beads and prayer-books.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Damn her ! that body of hers, While that my blood ran pure in 't, was more worth Than that which thou wouldst comfort, calFd a soul I will send her masks of common courtezans, Have her meat serv'd up by bawds and ruffians, And, 'cause she '11 needs be mad, I am resolv'd To move forth the common hospital All the mad-folk, and place them near her lodging ; There let them practise together, sing and dance, And act their gambols to the full o' the moon : If she can sleep the better for it, let her. Your work is almost ended.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Must I see her again ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Never.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You must.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Never in mine own shape ; That 's forfeited by my intelligence And this last cruel lie : when you send me next, The business shall be comfort.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Very likely; Thy pity is nothing of kin to thee. Antonio Lurks about Milan : thou shalt shortly thither, To feed a fire as great as my revenge, Which never will slack till it hath spent his fuel : Intemperate agues make physicians cruel.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: What hideous noise was that ?

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: 'Tis the wild consort Of madmen, lady, which your tyrant brother Hath plac'd about your lodging : this tyranny, I think, was never practis'd till this hour.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Indeed, I thank him : nothing but noise and folly Can keep me in my right wits ; whereas reason And silence make me stark mad. Sit down ; Discourse to me some dismal tragedy.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: O, 'twill increase your melancholy !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Thou art deceiv'd : To hear of greater grief would lessen mine. This is a prison ?

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Yes, but you shall live To shake this durance off.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Thou art a fool : The robin-red-breast and the nightingale Never live long in cages.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Pray, dry your eyes. What think you of, madam ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Of nothing; When I muse thus, I sleep.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Like a madman, with your eyes open ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Dost thou think we shall know one another In the other world ?

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Yes, out of question.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: O, that it were possible we might But hold some two days' conference with the dead ! From them I should learn somewhat, I am sure, I never shall know here. I '11 tell thee a miracle ; I am not mad yet, to my cause of sorrow : The heaven o'er my head seems made of molten brass, The earth of flaming sulphur, yet I am not mad. I am acquainted with sad misery As the tann'd galley-slave is with his oar ; Necessity makes me suffer constantly, And custom makes it easy. Who do I look like now ?

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Like to your picture in the gallery, A deal of life in show, but none in practice ; Or rather like some reverend monument Whose ruins are even pitied.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Very proper ; And Fortune seems only to have her eye-sight To behold my tragedy.— How now ! What noise is that ?

speeches.speaker: SERVANT
speeches.text: I am come to tell you Your brother hath intended you some sport. A great physician, when the Pope was sick Of a deep melancholy, presented him With several sorts of madmen, which wild object Being full of change and sport, forc'd him to laugh, And so the imposthume broke : the self-same cure The duke intends on you.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Let them come in.

speeches.speaker: SERVANT
speeches.text: There 's a mad lawyer ; and a secular priest ; A doctor that hath forfeited his wits By jealousy ; an astrologian That in his works said such a day o' the month Should be the day of doom, and, failing oft, Ran mad ; an English tailor craz'd i' the brain With the study of new fashions ; a gentleman-usher Quite beside himself with care to keep in mind The number of his lady's salutations Or * How do you ' she employ'd him in each morning ; A farmer, too, an excellent knave in grain, Mad 'cause he was hmdeiM transportation : And let one broker that 's mad loose to these, You 'd think the devil were among them.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Sit, Cariola. — Let them loose when you please, For I am chain'd to endure all your tyranny.

speeches.speaker: MADMAN
speeches.text: O, let us howl some heavy note, Some deadly dogged howl, Sounding as from the threatening throat Of beasts and fatal fowl ! As ravens, screech-owls, bulls, and bears, We '11 bell, and bawl our parts, Till irksome noise have cloy'd your ears And corrosiv'd your hearts. At last, whenas our quire wants breath, Our bodies being blest, We '11 sing, like swans, to welcome death, And die in love and rest.

speeches.speaker: FIRST MADMAN
speeches.text: Doom's-day not come yet ! I '11 draw it nearer by a perspective, or make a glass that shall set all the world on fire upon an instant. I cannot sleep ; my pillow is stuffed with a litter of porcupines.

speeches.speaker: SECOND MADMAN
speeches.text: Hell is a mere glass-house, where the devils are continually blowing up women's souls on hollow irons, and the fire never goes out.

speeches.speaker: THIRD MADMAN
speeches.text: I will lie with every woman in my parish the tenth night ; I will tythe them over like hay-cocks.

speeches.speaker: FOURTH MADMAN
speeches.text: Shall my pothecary out-go me because I am a cuckold ? I have found out his roguery ; he makes allum out of his wife's urine, and sells it to Puritans that have sore throats with over-straining.

speeches.speaker: FIRST MADMAN
speeches.text: I have skill in heraldry.

speeches.speaker: SECOND MADMAN
speeches.text: Hast?

speeches.speaker: FIRST MADMAN
speeches.text: You do give for your crest a woodcock's head with the brains picked out on't; you are a very ancient gentleman.

speeches.speaker: THIRD MADMAN
speeches.text: Greek is turned Turk : we are only to be saved by the Helvetian translation.

speeches.speaker: FIRST MADMAN
speeches.text: Come on, sir, I will lay the law to you.

speeches.speaker: SECOND MADMAN
speeches.text: O, rather lay a corrosive : the law will eat to the bone.

speeches.speaker: THIRD MADMAN
speeches.text: He that drinks but to satisfy nature is damned.

speeches.speaker: FOURTH MADMAN
speeches.text: If I had my glass here, I would show a sight should make all the women here call me mad doctor.

speeches.speaker: FIRST MADMAN
speeches.text: What 's he ? a rope-maker ?

speeches.speaker: SECOND MADMAN
speeches.text: No, no, no, a snuffling knave that, while he shows the tombs, will have his hand in a wench's placket.

speeches.speaker: THIRD MADMAN
speeches.text: Woe to the caroche that brought home my wife from the mask at three o'clock in the morning ! it had a large featherbed in it.

speeches.speaker: FOURTH MADMAN
speeches.text: I have pared the devil's nails forty times, roasted them in raven's eggs, and cured agues with them.

speeches.speaker: THIRD MADMAN
speeches.text: Get me three hundred milch-bats, to make possets to procure sleep.

speeches.speaker: FOURTH MADMAN
speeches.text: All the college may throw their caps at me : I have made a soap-boiler costive ; it was my masterpiece.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Is he mad too ?

speeches.speaker: SERVANT
speeches.text: Pray, question him. I '11 leave you.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I am come to make thy tomb.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Ha ! my tomb ! Thou speak'st as if I lay upon my death-bed, Gasping for breath : dost thou perceive me sick ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yes, and the more dangerously, since thy sickness is insensible.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Thou art not mad, sure : dost know me ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Who am I ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Thou art a box of worm-seed, at best but a salvatory of green mummy. What's this flesh ? a little crudded milk, fantastical puff-paste. Our bodies are weaker than those paper-prisons boys use to keep flies in ; more contemptible, since ours is to preserve earth-worms. Didst thou ever see a lark in a cage ? Such is the soul in the body : this world is like her little turf of grass, and the heaven o'er our heads like her looking-glass, only gives us a miserable knowledge of the small compass of our prison.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Am not I thy duchess?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Thou art some great woman, sure, for riot begins to sit on thy forehead (clad in gray hairs) twenty years sooner than on a merry milk-maid's. Thou sleepest worse than if a mouse should be forced to take up her lodging in a cat's ear : a little infant that breeds its teeth, should it lie with thee, would cry out, as if thou wert the more unquiet bedfellow.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I am Duchess of Malfi still.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: That makes thy sleep so broken : Glories, like glow-worms, afar off shine bright, But, look'd to near, have neither heat nor light.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Thou art very plain.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: My trade is to flatter the dead, not the living ; I am a tomb-maker.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: And thou comest to make my tomb ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yes. G

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Let me be a little merry : — of what stuff wilt thou make it ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Nay, resolve me first, of what fashion ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Why, do we grow fantastical on our deathbed ? do we affect fashion in the grave ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Most ambitiously. Princes' images on their tombs do not lie, as they were wont, seeming to pray up to heaven ; but with their hands under their cheeks, as if they died of the tooth-ache : they are not carved with their eyes fixed upon the stars ; but as their minds were wholly bent upon the world, the self-same way they seem to turn their faces.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Let me know fully therefore the effect Of this thy dismal preparation, This talk fit for a charnel.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Now I shall : — Here is a present from your princely brothers ; And may it arrive welcome, for it brings Last benefit, last sorrow.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Let me see it : I have so much obedience in my blood, I wish it in their veins to do them good.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: This is your last presence-chamber.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: O my sweet lady !

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Peace ; it affrights not me.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I am the common bellman That usually is sent to condemn'd persons The night before they suffer.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Even now thou said'st Thou wast a tomb-maker.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: 'Twas to bring you By degrees to mortification. Listen. Hark, now everything is still, The screech-owl and the whistler shrill Call upon our dame aloud, And bid her quickly don her shroud ! Much you had of land and rent ; Your length in clay 's now competent : A long war disturb'd your mind ; Here your perfect peace is sign'd. Of what is 't fools make such vain keeping ? Sin their conception, their birth weeping, Their life a general mist of error, Their death a hideous storm of terror. Strew your hair with powders sweet, Don clean linen, bathe your feet, And (the foul fiend more to check) A crucifix let bless your neck : 'Tis now full tide 'tween night and day ; End your groan, and come away.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Hence, villains, tyrants, murderers ! alas ! What will you do with my lady ? — Call for help.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: To whom ? to our next neighbours ? they are mad-folks.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Remove that noise.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Farewell, Cariola. In my last will I have not much to give : A many hungry guests have fed upon me ; Thine will be a poor reversion.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: I will die with her.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I pray thee, look thou giv'st my little boy Some syrup for his cold, and let the girl Say her prayers ere she sleep. Now what you please : What death?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Strangling ; here are your executioners.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: I forgive them : The apoplexy, catarrh, or cough o' the lungs, Would do as much as they do.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Doth not death fright you ?

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Who would be afraid on 't, Knowing to meet such excellent company In the other world ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yet, methinks, The manner of your death should much afflict you : This cord should terrify you.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Not a whit : What would it pleasure me to have my throat cut With diamonds ? or to be smothered With cassia ? or to be shot to death with pearls ? I know death hath ten thousand several doors For men to take their exits ; and 'tis found They go on such strange geometrical hinges, You may open them both ways : any way, for heaven-sake, So I were out of your whispering. Tell my brothers That I perceive death, now I am well awake, Best gift is they can give or I can take. I would fain put off my last woman's fault, I 'd not be tedious to you.

speeches.speaker: FIRST EXECUTIONER
speeches.text: We are ready.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Dispose my breath how please you ; but my body Bestow upon my women, will you ?

speeches.speaker: FIRST EXECUTIONER
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Pull, and pull strongly, for your able strength Must pull down heaven upon me : — Yet stay ; heaven-gates are not so highly arch'd As princes' palaces ; they that enter there Must go upon their knees .— Come, violent death, Serve for mandragora to make me sleep ! — Go tell my brothers, when I am laid out, They then may feed in quiet.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Where's the waiting- woman ? Fetch her : some other strangle the children. Look you, there sleeps your mistress.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: O, you are damn'd Perpetually for this ! My turn is next ; Is't not so order'd?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yes, and I am glad You are so well prepar'd for 't.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: You are deceiv'd, sir, I am not prepar'd for ?t, I will not die ; I will first come to my answer, and know How I have offended.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Come, despatch her. — You kept her counsel ; now you shall keep ours.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: I will not die, I must not ; I am contracted ' To a young gentleman. . , <

speeches.speaker: FIRST EXECUTIONER
speeches.text: Here 's your wedding-ring.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: Let me but speak with the duke. I '11 discover Treason to his person.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Delays :— throttle her.

speeches.speaker: FIRST EXECUTIONER
speeches.text: She bites and scratches.

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: If you kill me now, I am damn'd ; I have not been at confession This two years.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: When?

speeches.speaker: CARIOLA
speeches.text: I am quick with child.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Why, then, Your credit 's saved. Bear her into the next room ; Let these lie still.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Is she dead ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: She is what You'd have her. But here begin your pity : Alas, how have these offended ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: The death Of young wolves is never to be pitied.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Fix your eye here.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Constantly.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Do you not weep ? Other sins only speak ; murder shrieks out : The element of water moistens the earth, But blood flies upwards and bedews the heavens.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Cover her face ; mine eyes dazzle : she died young.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I think not so ; her infelicity Seem'd to have years too many.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: She and I were twins ; And should I die this instant, I had Hv'd Her time to a minute.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: It seems she was born first : You have bloodily approv'd the ancient truth, That kindred commonly do worse agree Than remote strangers.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Let me see her face Again. Why didst thou not pity her ? what An excellent honest man mightst thou have been, If thou hadst borne her to some sanctuary Or, bold in a good cause, oppos'd thyself, With thy advanced sword above thy head, Between her innocence and my revenge ! I bade thee, when I was distracted of my wits, Go kill my dearest friend, and thou hast done 't. For let me but examine well the cause : What was the meanness of her match to me ? Only I must confess I had a hope, Had she continu'd widow, to have gain'd An infinite mass of treasure by her death : And what was the main cause ? her marriage, That drew a stream of gall quite through my heart. For thee, as we observe in tragedies That a good actor many times is curs'd For playing a villain's part, I hate thee for't, And, for my sake, say, thou hast done much ill well.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Let me quicken your memory, for I perceive You are falling into ingratitude : I challenge The reward due to my service.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I '11 tell thee What I '11 give thee.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Do.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I '11 give thee a pardon For this murder.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Ha!

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Yes, and 'tis The largest bounty I can study to do thee. By what authority didst thou execute This bloody sentence ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: By yours.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Mine 1 was I her judge ? Did any ceremonial form of law Doom her to not-being ? did a c6mplete jury Deliver her conviction up i' the court ? Where shalt thou find this judgment register'd, Unless in hell ? See, like a bloody fool, Thou'st forfeited thy life, and thou shalt die for't.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: The office of justice is perverted quite When one thief hangs another. Who shall dare To reveal this ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: O, I '11 tell thee ; The wolf shall find her grave, and scrape it up, Not to devour the corpse, but to discover The horrid murder.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: You, not I, shall quake for 't.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Leave me.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I will first receive my pension.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You are a villain.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: When your ingratitude Is judge, I am so.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: O horror, That not the fear of him which binds the devils Can prescribe man obedience ! — Never look upon me more.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Why, fare thee well. Your brother and yourself are worthy men : You have a pair of hearts are hollow graves, Rotten, and rotting others ; and your vengeance, Like two chain'd bullets, still goes arm in arm : You may be brothers ; for treason, like the plague, Doth take much in a blood. I stand like one That long hath ta'en a sweet and golden dream : I am angry with myself, now that I wake.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Get thee into some unknown part o' the world, That I may never see thee.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Let me know Wherefore I should be thus neglected. Sir, I serv'd your tyranny, and rather strove To satisfy yourself than all the world : And though I loath'd the evil, yet I loVd You that did counsel it ; and rather sought To appear a true servant than an honest man.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I '11 go hunt the badger by owl-light : 'Tis a deed of darkness.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: He 's much distracted. Off, my painted honour While with vain hopes our faculties we tire, We seem to sweat in ice and freeze in fire. What would I do, were this to do again ? I would not change my peace of conscience For all the wealth of Europe.— She stirs; here's life :— Return, fair soul, from darkness, and lead mine Out of this sensible hell : — she 's warm, she breathes : — Upon thy pale lips I will melt my heart, To store them with fresh colour. — Who 's there ! Some cordial drink ! — Alas ! I dare not call : So pity would destroy pity. — Her eye opes, And heaven in it seems to ope, that late was shut, To take me up to mercy.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Antonio !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yes, madam, he is living ; The dead bodies you saw were but feign'd statues : He 's reconcil'd to your brothers ; the Pope hath wrought The atonement.

speeches.speaker: DUCHESS
speeches.text: Mercy !

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, she 's gone again ! there the cords of life broke. O sacred innocence, that sweetly sleeps On turtles' feathers, whilst a guilty conscience Is a black register wherein is writ All our good deeds and bad, a perspective That shows us hell ! That we cannot be suffered To do good when we have a mind to it ! This is manly sorrow ; These tears, I am very certain, never grew In my mother's milk : my estate is sunk Below the degree of fear : where were These penitent fountains while she was living ? O, they were frozen up ! Here is a sight As direful to my soul as is the sword Unto a wretch hath slain his father. Come, I '11 bear thee hence, And execute thy last will ; that 's deliver Thy body to the reverend dispose Of some good women : that the cruel tyrant Shall not deny me. Then I '11 post to Milan, Where somewhat I will speedily enact Worth my dejection.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: What think you of my hope of reconcilement To the Arragonian brethren ?

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I misdoubt it ; For though they have sent their letters of safe-conduct For your repair to Milan, they appear But nets to entrap you. The Marquis of Pescara, Under whom you hold certain land in cheat, Much 'gainst his noble nature hath been mov'd To seize those lands ; and some of his dependants Are at this instant making it their suit To be invested in your revenues. I cannot think they mean well to your life That do deprive you of your means of life, Your living.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You are still an heretic To any safety I can shape myself.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Here comes the marquis : I will make myself Petitioner for some part of your land, To know whither it is flying.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I pray, do.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Sir, I have a suit to you.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: To me ?

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: An easy one : There is the Citadel of Saint Bennet, With some demesnes, of late in the possession Of Antonio Bologna,— please you bestow them on me.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: You are my friend ; but this is such a suit, Nor fit for me to give, nor you to take.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: No, sir ?

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: I will give you ample reason for 't Soon in private :— here 's the cardinal's mistress.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: My lord, I am grown your poor petitioner, And should be an ill beggar, had I not A great man's letter here, the cardinal's, To court you in my favour.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: He entreats for you The Citadel of Saint Bennet, that belong'd To the banish'd Bologna.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: I could not have thought of a friend I could rather Pleasure with it : 'tis yours.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Sir, I thank you ; And he shall know how doubly I am engaged Both in your gift, and speediness of giving Which makes your grant the greater.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: How they fortify Themselves with my ruin I

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Sir, I am Little bound to you.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Why? .

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Because you denied this suit to me, and gave 't To such a creature.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Do you know what it was ? It was Antonio's land ; not forfeited By course of law, but ravish'd from his throat By the cardinal's entreaty : it were not fit I should bestow so main a piece of wrong Upon my friend ; 'tis a gratification Only due to a strumpet, for it is injustice. Shall I sprinkle the pure blood of innocents To make those followers I call my friends Look ruddier upon me ? I am glad This land, ta'en from the owner by such wrong, Returns again unto so foul an use As salary for his lust. Learn, good Delio, To ask noble things of me, and you shall find I '11 be a noble giver.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: You instruct me well.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Why, here's a man now would fright impudence From sauciest beggars.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Prince Ferdinand 's come to Milan, Sick, as they give out, of an apoplexy ; But some say 'tis a frenzy : I am going To visit him.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: 'Tis a noble old fellow.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: What course do you mean to take, Antonio ?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: This night I mean to venture all my fortune, Which is no more than a poor lingering life, To the cardinal's worst of malice : I have got Private access to his chamber ; and intend To visit him about the mid of night, As once his brother did our noble duchess. It may be that the sudden apprehension Of danger, — for I '11 go in mine own shape, — When he shall see it fraight with love and duty, May draw the poison out of him, and work A friendly reconcilement : if it fail, Yet it shall rid me of this imfamous calling ; For better fall once than be ever falling.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I '11 second you in all danger ; and howe'er, My life keeps rank with yours.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: You are still my lov'd and best friend.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Now, doctor, may I visit your patient ?

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: If 't please your lordship : but he 's instantly To take the air here in the gallery By my direction.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Pray thee, what 's his disease ?

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: A very pestilent disease, my lord, They call lycanthropia.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: What 's that ? I need a dictionary to 't.

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: I '11 tell you. In those that are possess'd with 't there o'erflows Such melancholy humour they imagine Themselves to be transformed into wolves ; Steal forth to church-yards in the dead of night, And dig dead bodies up : as two nights since One met the duke 'bout midnight in a lane Behind Saint Mark's church, with the leg of a man Upon his shoulder ; and he howl'd fearfully ; Said he was a wolf, only the difference Was, a wolfs skin was hairy on the outside, His on the inside ; bade them take their swords, H Rip up his flesh, and try : straight I was sent for, And, having minister'd to him, found his grace Very well recover'd.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: I am glad on 't.

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: Yet not without some fear Of a relapse. If he grow to his fit again, I '11 go a nearer way to work with him Than ever Paracelsus dream'd of ; if They '11 give me leave, I '11 buffet his madness out of him. Stand aside ; he comes.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Leave me.

speeches.speaker: MALATESTI
speeches.text: Why doth your lordship love this solitariness ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Eagles commonly fly alone : they are crows, daws, and starlings that flock together. Look, what 's that follows me ?

speeches.speaker: MALATESTI
speeches.text: Nothing, my lord.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: MALATESTI
speeches.text: 'Tis your shadow.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Stay it ; let it not haunt me.

speeches.speaker: MALATESTI
speeches.text: Impossible, if you move, and the sun shine.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I will throttle it.

speeches.speaker: MALATESTI
speeches.text: O, my lord, you are angry with nothing.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: You are a fool : how is 't possible I should catch my shadow, unless I fall upon 't ? When I go to hell, I mean to carry a bribe ; for, look you, good gifts evermore make way for the worst persons.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Rise, good my lord.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I am studying the art of patience.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Tis a noble virtue.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: To drive six snails before me from this town to Moscow ; neither use goad nor whip to them, but let them take their own time ;— the patient'st man i' the world match me for an experiment :— and I ' crawl after like a sheep-biter.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Force him up.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Use me well, you were best. What I have done, I have done : I '11 confess nothing.

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: Now let me come to him. — Are you mad, my lord ? are you out of your princely wits ?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: What 'she?

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Your doctor.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Let me have his beard sawed off, and his eye-brows filed more civil.

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: I must do mad tricks with him, for that 's the only way on 't. — I have brought your grace a salamander's skin to keep you from sun-burning.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: I have cruel sore eyes.

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: The white of a cockatrix's egg is present remedy.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Let it be a new-laid one, you were best. Hide me from him : physicians are like kings, — , They brook no contradiction.

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: Now he begins to fear me : now let me alone with him.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: How now ! put off your gown !

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: Let me have some forty urinals filled with rosewater : he and I '11 go pelt one another with them. — Now he begins to fear me. — Can you fetch a frisk, sir ? — Let him go, let him go, upon my peril : I find by his eye he stands in awe of me ; I '11 make him as tame as a dormouse.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
speeches.text: Can you fetch your frisks, sir ! — I will stamp him into a cullis, flay off his skin, to cover one of the anatomies this rogue hath set i1 the cold yonder in Barber-Chirurgeon's-hall. — Hence, hence ! you are all of you like beasts for sacrifice : there 's nothing left of you but tongue and belly, flattery and lechery.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Doctor, he did not fear you throughly.

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: True ; I was somewhat too forward.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Mercy upon me, what a fatal judgment Hath fall'n upon this Ferdinand !

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: Knows your grace What accident hath brought unto the prince This strange distraction ?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: I must feign somewhat. — Thus they say it grew. You have heard it rumour'd, for these many years None of our family dies but there is seen The shape of an old woman, which is given By tradition to us to have been murder'd By her nephews for her riches. Such a figure One night, as the prince sat up late at 's book, Appeared to him ; when crying out for help, The gentleman of 's chamber found his grace All on a cold sweat, alter'd much in face And language : since which apparition, He hath grown worse and worse, and I much fear He cannot live.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Sir, I would speak with you.

speeches.speaker: PESCARA
speeches.text: We '11 leave your grace, Wishing to the sick prince, our noble lord, All health of mind and body.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: You are most welcome. Are you come ? so. — This fellow must not know By any means I had intelligence In our duchess' death ; for, though I counsell'd it, The full of all the engagement seem'd to grow From Ferdinand. — Now, sir, how fares our sister? I do not think but sorrow makes her look Like to an oft-dy'd garment : she shall now Take comfort from me. Why do you look so wildly ? O, the fortune of your master here the prince Dejects you ; but be you of happy comfort : If you'll do one thing for me I '11 entreat, Though he had a cold tomb-stone o'er his bones, I 'd make you what you would be.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Any thing ; Give it me in a breath, and let me fly to 't : They that think long small expedition win, For musing much o} the end cannot begin.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Sir, will you come in to supper ?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: I am busy ; leave me. Julia What an excellent shape hath that fellow !

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: 'Tis thus. Antonio lurks here in Milan : Inquire him out, and kill him. While he lives, Our sister cannot marry ; and I have thought Of an excellent match for her. Do this, and style me Thy advancement.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: But by what means shall I find him out ?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: There is a gentleman call'd Delio Here in the camp, that hath been long approv'd His loyal friend. Set eye upon that fellow ; Follow him to mass ; may be Antonio, Although he do account religion But a school-name, for fashion of the world May accompany him ; or else go inquire out Delio's confessor, and see if you can bribe Him to reveal it. There are a thousand ways A man might find to trace him ; as to know What fellows haunt the Jews for taking up Great sums of money, for sure he 's in want ; Or else to go to the picture-makers, and learn Who bought her picture lately : some of these Happily may take.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Well, I '11 not freeze i' the business : I would see that wretched thing, Antonio, Above all sights i' the world.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Do, and be happy.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: This fellow doth breed basilisks in 's eyes, He 's nothing else but murder ; yet he seems Not to have notice of the duchess' death. 'Tis his cunning : I must follow his example ; There cannot be a surer way to trace Than that of an old fox.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: So, sir, you are well met.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: How now !

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Nay, the doors are fast enough : Now, sir, I will make you confess your treachery.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Treachery!

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Yes, confess to me Which of my women 'twas you hir'd to put Love-powder into my drink ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Love-powder !

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Yes, when I was at Malfi. Why should I fall in love with such a face else ? I have already suffer'd for thee so much pain, The only remedy to do me good Is to kill my longing.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Sure, your pistol holds Nothing but perfumes or kissing-comfits. Excellent lady ! You have a pretty way on 't to discover Your longing. Come, come, I '11 disarm you, And arm you thus : yet this is wondrous strange.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Compare thy form and my eyes together, You '11 find my love no such great miracle. Now you '11 say I am wanton : this nice modesty in ladies Is but a troublesome familiar That haunts them.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Know you me, I am a blunt soldier.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: The better: Sure, there wants fire where there are no lively sparks Of roughness.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: And I want compliment.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Why, ignorance In courtship cannot make you do amiss, If you have a heart to do well.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: You are very fair.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Nay, if you lay beauty to my charge, I must plead unguilty.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Your bright eyes Carry a quiver of darts in them sharper Than sun-beams.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: You will mar me with commendation, Put yourself to the charge of courting me, Whereas now I woo you.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I have it, I will work upon this creature. — Let us grow most amorously familiar : If the great cardinal now should see me thus, Would he not count me a villain ?

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: No ; he might count me a wanton, Not lay a scruple of offence on you ; For if I see and steal a diamond, The fault is not i' the stone, but in me the thief That purloins it. I am sudden with you : We that are great women of pleasure use to cut off These uncertain wishes and unquiet longings, And in an instant join the sweet delight And the pretty excuse together. Had you been i' the street, Under my chamber-window, even there I should have courted you.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, you are an excellent lady !

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Bid me do somewhat for you presently To express I love you.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I will ; and if you love me, Fail not to effect it. The cardinal is grown wondrous melancholy ; Demand the cause, let him not put you off With feign'd excuse ; discover the main ground on 't.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Why would you know this ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I have depended on him, And I hear that he is fall'n in some disgrace With the emperor : if he be, like the mice That forsake falling houses, I would shift To other dependance.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: You shall not need Follow the wars : I '11 be your maintenance.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: And I your loyal servant : but I cannot Leave my calling.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Not leave an ungrateful General for the love of a sweet lady ! You are like some cannot sleep in feather-beds, But must have blocks for their pillows.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Will you do this ?

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Cunningly.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: To-morrow I '11 expect the intelligence.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: To-morrow ! get you into my cabinet ; You shall have it with you. Do not delay me, No more than I do you : I am like one That is condemn'd ; I have my pardon promis'd, But I would see it seaPd. Go, get you in : You shall see me wind my tongue about his heart Like a skein of silk.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Where are you ?

speeches.speaker: SERVANTS
speeches.text: Here.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Let none, upon your lives, have conference With the Prince Ferdinand, unless I know it.— In this distraction he may reveal The murder. Yond 's my lingering consumption : I am weary of her, and by any means Would be quit of.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: How now, my lord ! what ails you ?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Nothing.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: O, you are much alter'd : Come, I must be your secretary, and remove This lead from off your bosom : what's the matter?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: I may not tell you.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Are you so far in love with sorrow You cannot part with part of it ? or think you I cannot love your grace when you are sad As well as merry ? or do you suspect I, that have a been a secret to your heart These many winters, cannot be the same Unto your tongue ?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Satisfy thy longing, — The only way to make thee keep my counsel Is, not to tell thee.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Tell your echo this, Or flatterers, that like echoes still report What they hear though most imperfect, and not me ; For if that you be true unto yourself, I '11 know.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Will you rack me ?

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: No, judgment shall Draw it from you : it is an equal fault, To tell one's secrets unto all or none.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: The first argues folly.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: But the last tyranny.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Very well : why, imagine I have committed Some secret deed which I desire the world May never hear of.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Therefore may not I know it ? You have conceal'd for me as great a sin As adultery. Sir, never was occasion For perfect trial of my constancy Till now : sir, I beseech you

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: You '11 repent it

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Never.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: It hurries thee to ruin : I '11 not tell thee. Be well advis'd, and think what danger 'tis To receive a prince's secrets : they that do, Had need have their breasts hoop'd with adamant To contain them. I pray thee, yet be satisfied ; Examine thine own frailty ; 'tis more easy To tie knots than unloose them : 'tis a secret That, like a fingering poison, may chance lie Spread in thy veins, and kill thee seven year hence.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Now you dally with me.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: No more ; thou shalt know it. By my appointment the great Duchess of Malfi And two of her young children, four nights since, Were strangl'd.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: O heaven ! sir, what have you done !

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: How now? how settles this? think you your bosom Will be a grave dark and obscure enough For such a secret ?

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: You have undone yourself, sir.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Why?

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: It lies not in me to conceal it.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: No? Come, I will swear you to 't upon this book.

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: Most religiously.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Kiss it Now you shall never utter it ; thy curiosity Hath undone thee : thou 'rt poison'd with that book ; Because I knew thou couldst not keep my counsel, I have bound thee to 't by death.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: For pity-sake, hold

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Ha, Bosola !

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: I forgive you This equal piece of justice you have done ; For I betray'd your counsel to that fellow : He over-heard it ; that was the cause I said It lay not in me to conceal it.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O foolish woman, Couldst thou not have poison'd him ?

speeches.speaker: JULIA
speeches.text: 'Tis weakness, Too much to think what should have been done. I go, I know not whither.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Wherefore com'st thou hither ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: That I might find a great man like yourself, Not out of his wits as the Lord Ferdinand, To remember my service.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: I '11 have thee hew'd in pieces.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Make not yourself such a promise of that life Which is not yours to dispose of.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Who plac'd thee here ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Her lust, as she intended.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Very well : Now you know me for your fellow-murderer.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: And wherefore should you lay fair marble colours Upon your rotten purposes to me ? Unless you imitate some that do plot great treasons, And when they have done, go hide themselves i' the grave Of those were actors in 't ?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: No more ; there is A fortune attends thee.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Shall I go sue to Fortune any longer ? 'Tis the fool's pilgrimage.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: I have honours in store for thce.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: There are many ways that conduct to seeming honour, And some of them very dirty ones.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Throw to the devil Thy melancholy. The fire burns well ; What need we keep a stirring oft, and make A greater smother ? Thou wilt kill Antonio ?

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Yes.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Take up that body.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: I think I shall Shortly grow the common bier for church-yards.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: I will allow thee some dozen of attendants To aid thee in the murder.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: O, by no means. Physicians that apply horse-leeches to any rank swelling use to cut off their tails, that the blood may run through them the faster : let me have no train when I go to shed blood, lest it make me have a greater when I ride to the gallows.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Come to me after midnight, to help to remove That body to her own lodging : I '11 give out She died o' the plague ; 'twill breed the less inquiry After her death.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Where's Castruccio her husband?

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: He 's rode to Naples, to take possession Of Antonio's citadel.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: Believe me, you have done a very happy turn.

speeches.speaker: CARDINAL
speeches.text: Fail not to come : there is the master-key Of our lodgings ; and by that you may conceive What trust I plant in you.

speeches.speaker: BOSOLA
speeches.text: You shall find me ready. 0 poor Antonio, though nothing be so needful To thy estate as pity, yet I find Nothing so dangerous ! I must look to my footing : In such slippery ice-pavements men had need To be frost-nail'd well, they may break their necks else ; The precedent 's here afore me. How this man Bears up in blood ! seems fearless ! Why, 'tis well ; Security some men call the suburbs of hell, Only a dead wall between. Well, good Antonio, 1 '11 seek thee out ; and all my care shall be To put thee into safety from the reach Of these most cruel biters that have got Some of thy blood already. It may be, I '11 join with thee in a most just revenge : The weakest arm is strong enough that strikes With the sword of justice. Still methinks the duchess Haunts me : there, there !— 'Tis nothing but my melancholy. O Penitence, let me truly taste thy cup, That throws men down only to raise them up !

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Yond 's the cardinal's window. This fortification Grew from the ruins of an ancient abbey ; And to yond side o' the river lies a wall, Piece of a cloister, which in my opinion Gives the best echo that you ever heard, So hollow and so dismal, and withal So plain in the distinction of our words, That many have suppos'd it is a spirit That answers.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: I do love these ancient ruins. We never tread upon them but we set Our foot upon some reverend history : And, questionless, here in this open court, Which now lies naked to the injuries Of stormy weather, some men lie interr'd Lov'd the church so well, and gave so largely to 't, They thought it should have canopied their bones Till dooms-day ; but all things have their end : Churches and cities, which have diseases like to men, Must have like death that we have.

speeches.speaker: ECHO
speeches.text: Like death that we have.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Now the echo hath caught you.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: It groan'd methought, and gave A very deadly accent.

speeches.speaker: ECHO
speeches.text: Deadly accent.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: I told you 'twas a pretty one : you may make it A huntsman, or a falconer, a musician, Or a thing of sorrow.

speeches.speaker: ECHO
speeches.text: A thing of sorrow.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: Ay, sure, that suits it best.

speeches.speaker: ECHO
speeches.text: That suits it best.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
speeches.text: 'Tis very like my wife's voice.

speeches.speaker: ECHO
speeches.text: Ay, wifjs voice.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Come, let us walk further from 't. I would not have you go to the cardinal's to-night : Do not.

speeches.speaker: ECHO
speeches.text: Do not.

speeches.speaker: DELIO
speeches.text: Wisdom doth not more moderate wasting sorrow Than time: take time for't; be mindful of thy safety.

speeches.speaker: ECHO
